item.title: UK houses near top state secondary schools cost £40,000 more, research reveals
item.author: Rob Davies
item.content:encoded: Premium of nearly 10% paid by housebuyers comparable with cost of a cheaper private school over seven yearsA house near a top state secondary school costs an extra £40,000 on average, according to research that reveals education premiums that rank alongside some private school fees.The average property in a postcode district that includes a top 50 state secondary commands a price tag of £415,791, compared with £375,217 across the wider local authority areas in which those schools are located, a UK-wide analysis by the estate agent Yopa found.Continue reading...

item.title: Burnham to Address UK Parliament as MPs Return From Summer Break
item.author: Joe Mayes
item.content:encoded: After a political honeymoon of good vibes and voter-friendly announcements, the return of Parliament means that the UK’s new prime minister, Andy Burnham, must confront hard choices that lie ahead.

item.title: Bessent Faces G20 Credibility Test Amid Interventions
item.content:encoded: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s interventionist summer has already led to pushback and questions about his credibility in financial markets. Now he faces a test with global peers. Ahead of the meeting of Group of 20 finance ministers in Asheville, North Carolina, on Monday, Bessent has vowed to return the conversation among the world’s top economic policymakers to the core subject of boosting growth. The challenge for Bessent in selling this message is that the biggest threats to global growth this year have come from the high energy prices and other consequences of President Donald Trump’s war on Iran, as well as the impact of US tariffs that are again in focus with the launch of a new trade war against fellow G20 member Canada. Bloomberg Senior Economics Writer Shawn Donnan joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. He speaks with Tim Stenovec and Kristine Aquino. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Airbnb Rolls Out Pilot Program in US to Lower Fees Paid by Hosts to 6% or 10%

The 2,193-mile trail runs between Springer Mountain in Georgia and Mount Katahdin in Maine.Continue reading...

item.title: Knicks Domino Effects: What if Jalen Brunson stayed in Dallas?
item.author: Michael Zeno
item.content:encoded: Domino effects are meant to start relatively small. The first two editions of the series, I feel like, encompassed that. We got really niche with the Mike Brown Kings saga and less niche with Julius Randle’s injury, but both of them required a lot of outside-the-box thinking to see directly what a reversal would’ve caused to the Knicks’ long-term hopes.This one is anything but niche.To wrap up this mini-series I’ve had fun with over the dog days of the summer, we’re going to look at possibly the biggest domino effect of them all, one that was scarily realistic and only didn’t occur because of the hubris of a certain front office that later made one of the worst trades in NBA history.You saw the title. This is a scenario that Jalen Brunson, the birthday boy and the man who has exceeded every expectation and has spearheaded a revival of Knicks basketball so grand that all of us have spent way too much money on championship merch, never puts on the orange and blue.Following his third season in Dallas, Brunson and his agents at CAA wanted to negotiate a contract extension with the Mavericks’ brass. The number that they decided on was more than reasonable for a player of his current production: four years and $55 million. After all, he was coming off finishing fourth in Sixth Man of the Year voting with plausible upward mobility. Dallas said no. Fast forward a few months: as Brunson began what turned out to be a breakout campaign, he and his agent approached the Mavs again about the same framework and were again told no. Brunson kept working and gradually improving to the point where the Mavs themselves approached him about the $55 million deal after the trade deadline, but at that point, he had outgrown that offer as he was barreling towards free agency. Four months later, he landed in New York on a four-year, $104 million pact.But what if Dallas realized what they had in Brunson at either one of those points, particularly the in-season extension? What if they took a guy that the Knicks had long been looking at off the market? Such a deal would’ve been more than reasonable for their current cap structure as a sixth man or starter next to Luka Doncic, even if the fit was potentially difficult due to both of their defensive shortcomings. Frankly, it was nonsensical for them to be that blind. This was a good player.December 1, 2021. Jalen Brunson and the Dallas Mavericks announce a four-year, $55 million extension that will begin the following season. Let’s see where the dominoes fall.Nothing changes from this point forward on any side for the rest of the 2021-22 season. Brunson still balls out and gets on the national radar with his incredible performance in the postseason; the Knicks still miss the playoffs, etc. Instead of the media clowning the Knicks for giving Brunson a nine-figure deal in June, the offseason is spent lauding Nico Harrison and company for their wherewithal to lock down this impact player for cheap.Of course, this creates a gigantic path of divergence for the Knicks, who were always infatuated with Brunson because of his family connections. I still think Rick Brunson gets hired onto Tom Thibodeau’s staff to replace the outgoing Kenny Payne (who had a truly disastrous tenure at Louisville). The hiring was definitely motivated by his son’s free agency, but he had also served as an assistant under Thibs in Chicago and Minnesota, so it still happens.The real question, though, is what happens in that offseason. Our first major question revolves around the strategy for the 2022 NBA Draft, particularly with the No. 11 overall pick.For those who don’t remember, the Knicks selected Ousmane Dieng, traded him to the Thunder in exchange for three first-round picks, traded up to No. 13 in exchange for two picks, selected Jalen Duren, and shipped him to Detroit alongside Kemba Walker in an effective salary dump. The team came out with solid assets and cleared up some cash.The motivation behind punting a lottery pick? Signing Jalen Brunson. A later trade with Detroit shipped Alec Burks and Nerlens Noel to the Motor City and cleared up just enough space for the Villanova alum and Isaiah Hartenstein in free agency. It’s why I never cared about people saying “the Knicks traded Jalen Duren for nothing” because it’s false. You don’t get Brunson (most likely) without trading Duren, his cap hit, and the salary attached. But with Brunson off the table and no clear reason to use cap space, the Knicks are dead set on picking in the lottery. You might think it’s as simple as drafting Dieng or Duren, but the Knicks almost certainly made both selections on behalf of the teams they were actively negotiating with. After all, if they wanted them, they wouldn’t trade them.There were a few plans for this draft leading up to it. After the Knicks were once again denied a chance at lottery luck, they constantly rang the phones to try to trade up for Jaden Ivey. They may get over the line for this. After all, with no Brunson on the way, there are no schematic issues.It would still be a very difficult trade to make, so I lean toward it not happening. After Ivey, they seemed quite enamored with Wisconsin guard Johnny Davis, but the Wizards took him 10th overall. That’s two major bullets dodged, but who’s on the clock at No. 11?The available players who had a pre-draft workout in New York were AJ Griffin, Tari Eason, MarJon Beauchamp, and Mark Williams. I would think it would be one of these guys, even if the extremely talented Jalen Williams and Duren were on the board. In typical Leon Rose fashion, he probably does the first two trades of the night, where he trades out and comes back in, ultimately scooping up two conditional firsts from Detroit and Washington while trading four seconds. With the 13th pick, they select Duke wing AJ Griffin.With no Brunson and an unsuccessful pursuit of both Davis and Ivey in the draft, the Knicks badly need a point guard. I’d assume they still look to offload salary, particularly with Kemba, to open cap space, but the extent of this is unclear due to the lack of a clear alternative in free agency. There’s restricted free agent Collin Sexton, of course, but the direction that needs to be taken appears to be in the trade market. Fortunately, there are two lead guards available.Dejounte Murray is on the block in San Antonio and could be had for a reasonable package. His defensive fortitude makes him a welcome fit for a team that has major defensive questions, and his offense has also proven capable of a leap forward. There’s also that New York native out in Utah who could be of use…For Murray, the Knicks never seemed that motivated to make that move, even if he would’ve been a decent fit next to Brunson in real life. They were always more focused on adding Donovan Mitchell and figuring it out later. In this timeline, Murray still goes to Atlanta, but it’s a full-court press on bringing Spida home.With no Brunson, there’s nothing holding them back from adding a small guard into the fray. The fit concerns aren’t there. When Danny Ainge and the Jazz ask for a ridiculous package, it’s eventually negotiated down into something the team can agree on. In mid-August 2022, Mitchell comes home for a package centered around RJ Barrett and Quentin Grimes, depleting the team’s draft capital to keep further players out of the deal. As much as fans want to play the kids, the Knicks see an opportunity to compete and take it.Thus, here’s the rotation we have heading into the 2022-23 season:Donovan Mitchell – Derrick RoseEvan Fournier – Immanuel QuickleyAlec Burks – Cam Reddish/AJ GriffinJulius Randle – Obi ToppinMitchell Robinson – Isaiah HartensteinYes, in this reality, we assume that the Knicks still find a way to get off Noel’s contract but keep Burks as wing depth after trading Barrett and Grimes. Hartenstein was always a target for the front office and still comes to New York.This lineup, as you might imagine, would’ve been rather erratic. You have some brilliant shotmakers in there, but not enough defenders. Tom Thibodeau’s seat gets hot again; he’s forced to bench some players permanently, and the mini-revival still happens… to an extent.Quickley gets a chance to start with Spida, Deuce McBride’s emergence happens a year sooner, Randle enjoys his bounce-back season. The foundation of the start of the Brunson era would’ve likely been similar, but the real repercussions come later.At the deadline, the team needs wing depth, having iced Reddish out of the rotation. With Brunson no longer on the team, I can’t imagine the interest in Josh Hart is any more pronounced. It’s still possible that the trade happens. I’m instead going to involve the Knicks in the multi-team trade with the Warriors and Pistons that got Gary Payton II back to the Bay. The Knicks send a bucket of seconds and Cam Reddish to Detroit for Saddiq Bey.With Mitchell, the Knicks win 48 games and slide into the fourth seed in the Eastern Conference, where they host a Cavs team that never got the New York native and instead had to continue building around Darius Garland, Sexton, and Evan Mobley. The Knicks still win in five.In the second round, the Bucks still get slayed by the wrath of Jimmy Butler and the Heat, and although many fans are optimistic about the prospects of facing the No. 8 seed, Butler waxes the Knicks in a six-game defeat.Heading into the following season, the Knicks are content with what they got, planning to use it as a building year. Burks never being traded means there’s not enough space to sign Donte DiVincenzo, who was also likely going to be someone Brunson pitched signing. There’s no big move to be made here, so we keep going into a shaky start to the 2023-24 season, which leaves them at an inflection point around the New Year.As you might recall, OG Anunoby was acquired in real life on December 30, 2023, for RJ Barrett, Immanuel Quickley, and a second-round pick. In this reality, Barrett is already gone, but Quickley is becoming a foundational piece after being started out of necessity midway through the prior season. The financials still work if the Knicks add Burks to the trade, but with Barrett not included, the rest of the team’s excess draft capital goes with it.The Big 3 of Spida-Anunoby-Randle destroy the competition in January 2024 until injuries take out both Randle and Anunoby. Mitchell does his best to imitate 2024 Brunson and gets First-Team All-NBA for his troubles, but it’s certainly an uphill climb. Without DiVincenzo to help with off-ball scoring, the Knicks only win 46 games, dropping them to the play-in tournament. Remember, the No. 2 and No. 7 seeds were just three games apart that year.The Knicks get revenge on the Heat in the 7-8 game, but have to fare with a road series against Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Bucks in the first round, one that just doesn’t go well. With no Randle to physically match up, Toppin (who I believe doesn’t get traded with the team’s worst depth the prior season) and Precious Achiuwa are overwhelmed in a six-game defeat. The front office blames injuries and doesn’t make any drastic moves… yet.The Mikal Bridges trade never happens. They had to use a boatload of draft assets to get Anunoby and Mitchell, so the Nets aren’t interested. Anunoby extends, Spida gets his three-year, $150 million extension, and the Knicks seem prepared to run it back in 2024-25.Now, you might wonder: what about KAT?The Knicks badly wanted him, but they lacked a guy who Minnesota really valued in DiVincenzo to get it done. Further, the fact that Mitchell took a max extension puts the team eerily close to the second apron, something they avoided with Brunson’s pay cut. There’s a very realistic world that this trade doesn’t happen, but Leon Rose always gets his guy, so they trade Mitchell Robinson and the last bits of draft capital to get it done.It’s not worth prognosticating who fills the Hart and Bridges gaps in the lineup, but the Knicks are built around Mitchell, Anunoby, and Towns. That Big 3 would get two seasons to work everything out, going into the second apron in 2025-26 before James Dolan would order a restructuring. They had to win. They had no choice. In the first year, they get bounced in the second round by the Celtics after a 52-win season. The poise of the Brunson-led Knicks was a big part of why they came back from all those deficits, plus the team would be utterly devoid of defensive length without Robinson or Bridges. This also means that the Knicks and Pacers never rekindle their rivalry in either season, which is fun to think about.In 2025-26, the year we all rejoiced in real life, they had a real chance. They fortified the depth; they hired Mike Brown to replace Thibs; they waltzed into an extremely weak East and grabbed the bull by the horns.50 wins in the regular season, enough for the No. 3 seed. They survived a seven-game war with Atlanta, took out Philadelphia in six games, and went face-to-face with the Pistons in the ECF. Remember, no Mitchell likely dooms the Cavs to mediocrity and no ECF berth. It’s hard to say for sure if the Pistons give the Knicks the same fits they did in real life, but let’s look at the facts. The Knicks were still a major question mark defensively and had no answer for Cade Cunningham. Additionally, they lacked the presence of Robinson (even in a backup role) to fluster Duren. In a tense, seven-game series, the Pistons prevailed. It’s over.Mitchell would not be extended again by the Knicks, as his playoff shortcomings would not be worth the $270 million extension he got in real life. I’d think the front office would side with the Big Bodega in this, and the team would be built around the fleeting prime of Towns from here.Safe to say, no banners. Sad stuff. But how’s Jalen doing in Dallas?Brunson’s New Life In DallasDallas did basically nothing that offseason to replace Brunson, leaving them inherently weaker entering the 2022-23 season. They still acquire Christian Wood after retaining Brunson, but they feel pretty stagnant.The big change in the 2022-23 season is that the Mavericks never traded for Kyrie Irving, as the fit with him, Brunson, and Luka would’ve been quite bizarre. They also wouldn’t feel the need to, as when Doncic goes down with injury right before the deadline, we see glimpses of Knicks Brunson in the emerging Villanova alum.Dallas was quite bad this season, flaming out in the play-in tournament, but an interesting trickle-down effect from this is that they wouldn’t be able to properly tank to keep their draft pick, so a parting gift from Brunson would give the Knicks a lottery pick in 2023, which they’d use on a guy like Jordan Hawkins. Not a needle mover, so I didn’t feel the need to mention until now.The reverb would be no Dereck Lively II in Dallas, but the supporting cast from guys like PJ Washington and eventually Daniel Gafford would provide enough for the Mavericks to still go deep in the postseason in 2024, maybe making the NBA Finals but still not coming that close to a title.At the same time that all appears to be well in Dallas, Nico Harrison is stirring. He doesn’t like the frequent unavailability of Doncic, who still suffers a major hamstring injury on Christmas 2024. In his absence, unlike in real life where Kyrie suffered a multi-week injury as well, the Mavericks experience the joy of 2024 Jalen Brunson, who carries Dallas through January to the point where Harrison has an epiphany.“What if I fortify my defense and Jalen can give me Luka-esque production?”Brunson’s explosion dooms Doncic’s tenure, as the controversial trade with the Lakers still occurs. Anthony Davis would now be paired with a head of the snake in Brunson, a match seemingly made in heaven.Except Davis is still injury-prone. Dallas never has the death spiral they had with Davis and Irving’s season-ending injuries because Brunson would be there trying to play hero ball. He does just enough to win them 45 games to take the No. 9 seed. After defeating Sacramento in the 9-10 game, a heroic 40-ball sees them stun the Grizzlies to steal a playoff spot, only to get eviscerated by the powerhouse Thunder.This turns out to be an utter disaster, as Cooper Flagg will no longer become a Maverick. It was possible to have a core of Brunson, Davis, and Flagg, but now? Brunson hits his 30th birthday with Davis shipped to Washington and a band of merrymen around him.That’s right. The real twist of all of this? Nobody wins.The Knicks lose because they don’t have Brunson. They never sniff the NBA Finals.The Mavericks lose because the domino effect takes two lottery picks away, and JB’s hyper-competitiveness doesn’t allow them to get younger.Jalen Brunson loses. Instead of being the King of New York, he’s got a microscope on him in lowly Dallas as the guy Nico traded Luka to feature.It’s a lose-lose situation. What a nightmare. I need my nightlight; someone turn on some highlights.That’s better. Happy Birthday, Cap. We’re so glad this never happened.

item.title: 'I'm pinching myself' - Ella Sabo replaces stress with demonstration of patience and power for podium finish at Philadelphia Cycling Classic
item.author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
item.content:encoded: The banner year for 20-year-old Ella Sabo (Virginia’s Blue Ridge TWENTY28) kept on rolling Sunday with a surprising podium finish at the Philadelphia Cycling Classic p/b AmeriGas. She exhibited her maturity and "multi-faceted" racing skills to be part of a chasing group which caught a late breakaway and saved enough in the tank across three hilly circuits of Lemon Hill to sprint for third.While two Women's WorldTour riders reached the finish line at Ben Franklin Parkway just a bike length sooner - Chiara Consonni (Canyon-SRAM) winning and Alexandra Volstad (EF Education-Oatly) going second - Sabo secured her best finish at a UCI one-day race. From the bunch sprint, she outpaced compatriot Kristen Faulkner (EF Education-Oatly) and three other WorldTour riders.Her Continental team was one of four squads with only four riders at the race, and they had to start minus Marlies Mejías due to sickness. So Sabo had only Olivia Cummins, Sofía Arreola, and Kenna Pfeiffer for support, while other teams brought six riders each."Coming into this week, we had to kind of shift gears pretty last minute with Marlies not feeling well, unfortunately, and so a bit of a last-minute change, and so it was a little stressful, I'll be honest, going into the race," Sabo told media, including , at the finish."I mean, it's unreal. I feel like I'm still trying to soak it all in. I'm pinching myself."The California native came into the restored Philly Classic, which had not been contested for the past 10 years, without personal knowledge of the tricky course, which included multiple passes of the 17% gradient of the Manayunk Wall. However, she had weapons based on experience from team staff - Shelley Olds, who was twice on the podium when the race was the Liberty Classic, and Giana Chilcott (nee Roberge), who directed the Saturn team to wins at the race. Also, Arreola most recently raced at the 2016 edition."She was like, it'll be a hard race, these girls want it," Sabo said about advice from Arreola. "They've been racing a different style of race that we're used to here in the U.S. We knew it was going to be aggressive, and we knew we were just going to have to be smart with what moves we followed."Arreola had also told her teammates about the tough climb in the Manayunk neighbourhood, on the far side of the Philadelphia circuit with the tough pitch from the Schuylkill river."I had been working in training, doing like two and a half minute efforts, specifically for that climb. So going into it, knowing I had put in the work in preparation to get myself up and over it, and hopefully contest a sprint. It was really cool to [see it] pay off."Having a squad of four versus some of these squads of six, it was going to be a challenge. So she [Arreola] made sure that we all soaked it in - just take in the atmosphere that is the Philly Cycling Classic, enjoy the environment. "That 'Wall', so many people cheering. It was so insane, so cool."Last year, Sabo won the USPro U23 national championship in the road race and this year she took the stars-and-stripes jersey in the U23 criterium national championship. And just prior to racing in Philadelphia, she came away from her first USA Cycling Elite Track Championships event with three gold medals - two in U23 individual races and one in the elite Women's Team Pursuit.The stakes were bigger for Sunday's international contest. A podium may have been a surprise to many people, but not to Nicola Cranmer, her team's executive director."In Philadelphia, Ella raced with tremendous patience. We only had four riders, and they did everything they could to keep her safe and in position until the final lap. From there, she was able to trust her instincts and race to the finish. She has a powerful sprint, and when the opportunity came, she really stepped up," Cranmer told ."Ella joined our team as a junior, and development takes patience. We’ve watched her make steady progress over the past few years, but this season she really came into her own with another level of confidence and maturity."Ella will remain with the team next year, and we’re really excited to see what she can do with even more opportunities."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Ask Pinstripe Alley: Yankees mailbag questions request
item.author: Madison Pavich
item.content:encoded: The Yankees completed their homestand this weekend with about as good of a result as you could ask for. After dropping two of three to Houston and getting just one run scored in the finale of that series, Friday’s 1-0 nailbiter of a win against Boston and subsequent shutout loss to them on the first game of a doubleheader on Saturday brought back concerns of their stagnant offense. However, they ripped through the final two games, scoring nine in the nightcap to split the doubleheader before blasting their way to 16 runs in the finale on Sunday to take the series and the season record against Boston. They now stand four games up on the Red Sox in the standings, but with that tiebreaker in hand they’ve got an extra game of protection should these two teams remain in the top Wild Card slots and face off to start October.The final month of the season is now in front of them, and they’ve got both a sizeable gap on Boston to uphold while also facing a nearly-identical gap between them and Tampa Bay for first place. Their penultimate series of the season lines them up to deal with that problem head-on, but if the deficit isn’t more than a game or two by then the odds of totally flipping the standings are negligible. Is the offensive eruption they had this weekend a sign of the lineup finally clicking, or will the droughts keep popping up? Was Will Warren’s performance in the finale the best start he’s had in his career, and can he follow it up with more down the stretch? How much are you expecting from Aaron Judge as he gears up to jump straight back into an MLB lineup without rehab games? If you have questions like these, or anything else on your mind, send ‘em in for a chance to be featured in our Yankees mailbag.Answers will run on Friday afternoon. All questions received by the night of September 3rd will be considered. You can leave your submissions in the comment section below or by e-mail to pinstripealleyblog [at] gmail [dot] com.

item.title: Tadej Pogačar's clavical surgery 'went well' Monday as team confirms World Champion will remain in Barcelona for several days
item.author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
item.content:encoded: Reigning world champion Tadej Pogačar had surgery Monday for a fractured collarbone sustained on stage 8 of the Vuelta a España. The medical director for UAE Team Emirates-XRG confirmed the procedure was "successful" and Pogačar would remain in a Barcelona hospital for a portion of this week to begin recovery.“This afternoon, Tadej underwent successful surgery on his left clavicle after receiving the all-clear to proceed with the operation. The procedure went well and he will remain in hospital for post-operative monitoring for a few days," Dr. Adrian Rotunno, the medical director for UAE Team Emirates-XRG, stated on the team's social media."When ready, Tadej will travel home to begin his recovery and rehabilitation under the supervision of the team’s medical staff. We will continue to monitor his progress closely throughout the recovery process."Having won three of the first six stages at this year's Vuelta and wearing the leader's jersey, Pogačar crashed in the middle of the peloton with 32km to go on Saturday's stage. He departed the race in an ambulance, his left shoulder heavily padded in a sling, later diagnosed with a concussion, displaced left clavicle fracture, a stable C7 cervical fracture, and multiple abrasions. Upon arrival to hospital in Barcelona, Pogačar posted a photo of himself wearing a soft neck brace and showing bandages to his face and hand, using the music to Bee Gees' 'Stayin Alive' to convey a positive vibe. The team has not confirmed any details about how the crash happened, there was speculation that the Slovenian may have swerved and gone down hard after hitting a small rock. For now, the quest to complete the sweep of Grand Tour GC titles is over for this season, as the Vuelta a España is the only one of the three he has not won yet. Pogačar has five Tour de France victories and one win at the Giro d'Italia. In question is his health status to race September 27 for a third road race World Championship.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.author: Brad Bourque
item.content:encoded: While memory and storage prices are still high, there are still good discounts on other gaming-related hardware. Take , for example. Dell is selling it for $319.99, a $30 break from the usual price of $349.99. The 27-inch gaming monitor features an QD-OLED panel for deep, immersive black levels, and quantum dots for full and vivid colors. With a 240Hz refresh rate for super smooth gaming, and AMD FreeSync Premium Plus to keep your frames per second and refresh rate locked together, this monitor is a great, budget-friendly choice for PC gamers who don’t want to compromise on contrast and fast response times.Connectivity is a bit limited, with a DisplayPort 1.4 port that supports up to 240Hz at 2560 x 1440, and two HDMI ports that support up to 120Hz at its peak resolution. While some other screens have USB hubs or audio connections, they aren’t necessary for PC gaming, and sometimes add to the cost. The included stand has adjustable swivel, height, pivot, and tilt, with a 100 x 100 VESA mount in case you want to mount it to a monitor arm or use a different stand. It also sports a lengthy three year warranty with coverage for burn-in.

Through 49.1 innings pitched, however, Schreiber’s strikeout (17.7 percent) and walk (10.8 percent) numbers raise some questions that aren’t exactly reassuring for the September playoff push.This move will hopefully allow relievers David Bednar, Brent Headrick, and Paul Blackburn to take some much-needed rest after exhausting their efforts in the last few series against the Blue Jays, Astros, and Red Sox.Schreiber first went to Kansas City in 2024 in a trade with the Red Sox for David Sandlin. He initially made his MLB debut with the Tigers in 2019 and spent two seasons with the team before he was claimed by Boston. With the postseason looming, this move has the potential to work out well for the Yankees after losing both Fernando Cruz and Ryan Weathers to the IL. item.title: Trump tells FCC to punish journalist for calling his election results "mixed"
item.author: Jon Brodkin
item.content:encoded: President Trump yesterday demanded that the Federal Communications Commission punish or rebuke an NBC journalist for saying he has "mixed results" in his election endorsements. In the latest example of how Trump is using the FCC to harass reporters and news organizations that he dislikes, he said host Kristen Welker "will be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment" for what he claimed was a "purposeful inaccuracy.""Kristen Welker, the Unpopular 'Hostess' of the once great Meet the Press, now considered Meet the Fake Press, just stated that Donald Trump has 'mixed results' on his Endorsements of Candidates, when the recent WINS of Darline Graham and Mike Mazzei, stand at 100% for the U.S. Senate, and 98% for the U.S. House, recently and over the longterm. How can anyone be allowed to say this, working for freely given Public Airwaves? Results are attached. Because of this purposeful inaccuracy, she will be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment," Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.A separate post from Trump yesterday said, "THE FAKE POLLS USED BY OUR CROOKED MEDIA ARE OUT OF CONTROL, AND SOMETHING MUST BE DONE ABOUT IT. FCC TO THE RESCUE! President DJT." Trump also posted a rant on Friday about New York Times journalist Maggie Haberman, calling her "an unattractive person both inside and out" who "should be forced to turn over any and all money that she’s made through her fake reporting on me." Trump referred to Haberman throughout his post as "Maggot Haberman."

item.title: Rising star Liam Slock deemed a 'powerful rider' set to strengthen Bahrain Victorious for next two seasons
item.content:encoded: Breakout Belgian rider Liam Slock has signed with Bahrain Victorious for two years, the team announced Monday. The 25-year-old has had an eye-catching season with Lotto-Intermarché, securing his first professional win at GP Gippingen in June, in a dramatic finish that saw him hit the deck on the approach to the finish line. Slock's arrival to Bahrain will bolster the team's strength in one-day racing and Grand Tours, with his power and versatility providing a great asset both in terms of team support, and his own potential chances, as he continues his development.“This is a new step in my career, and I am immensely looking forward to developing further in this new environment at Bahrain Victorious. I am motivated to bring my experience and qualities and to strengthen the Classics group of the team," Slock said of his move.“At the same time, I want to thank Lotto for the past six years. I learned a huge amount there, was given great opportunities, and grew both as a rider and as a person. I am grateful for the people and experiences I take with me from this period, and I look forward with confidence to what the future brings.”The move to Bahrain Victorious should see the Belgian continuing to make impressions at the WorldTour level. He made an impactful debut at the Tour de France, notching a number of breakaway efforts including a 40km solo attempt on stage 8 that saw him caught by the charging peloton just 1.3 kilometres from the finish line. He wasn't empty-handed, coming away with the most combative rider prize for the effort.Slock is the second rider confirmed to be departing from the Belgian side following the announcement that Arnaud de Lie would be moving to Tudor Pro Cycling from 2027, and other key names from the squad may also be heading elsewhere, with Lennert van Eetvelt reportedly on the way to NSN. Slock links with former Lotto teammate Alec Segaert at Bahrain, his younger compatriot who has had an excellent season since joining the team, including recording his first Grand Tour stage win at the Giro d'Italia in May.The team's performance manager Rod Ellingworth had this to say, on his new recruit: “We are very happy to add a powerful rider like Liam to our roster. He is a valuable addition who brings strength to all areas of our race programme, from one day races to stage races.“His arrival is part of Bahrain Victorious’ continued effort to strengthen our core engine for stage races and the Spring Classics. We believe Liam has the qualities and mentality to play an important role in our team and we are looking forward to seeing him develop further with us.”For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to . item.title: Raindrops are tiny lightning bolts, and they’re corroding cars, study finds
item.author: Jacek Krywko
item.content:encoded: The standard explanation for why rain causes corrosion is that water carries dissolved salts and acids to a surface, constant drumming of raindrops abrades whatever protective coating is on it, and oxygen does the rest. Nearly all our tools to prevent this—paints, polymer films, or oxide layers—are built around this idea. But we’ve apparently been missing something important about the rain.A new study led by Zhongyuan Ni, Rüdiger Berger, and Hans-Jürgen Butt at the Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research in Mainz, Germany, has shown that water drops routinely arrive at a surface carrying an electrical charge large enough to punch through an insulating coating. Not scratch it. Not slowly dissolve it. Electrically blow a hole in it, the way a spark jumps a gap.The starting point of the study is a phenomenon called "slide electrification," which has only been properly quantified in the past few years. When a water drop slides across an insulating surface like a leaf, a painted wall, a windowpane, or a plastic panel, it strips charge from that surface and leaves an opposing charge behind. The voltages involved are not trivial. Drops charged this way have been measured at up to 9,000 volts.

It was a clever way to describe the company’s approach to users’ attention and data. But the sharpness of her words was not matched by the deal. While the strengthening of child safety features is welcome, the tech giant once again batted off efforts to alter its products.Meta’s decision to settle enabled it to avoid any admission of liability. It put a stop to the awkward questions being asked of witnesses including Adam Mosseri, Instagram’s CEO, and the damaging claims made by whistleblowers such as Arturo Béjar. This former Meta safety engineer told the court that his own daughter had been sent unsolicited photos of male genitals on Instagram.Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? item.title: On MLB’s most recent CBA proposals
item.author: John Griffin
item.content:encoded: This past Thursday, Major League Baseball made its latest round of proposals to the Players’ Association, this type focusing on so-called “roster stability.” Claiming that roster churn during both the season and offseason makes it difficult for fans to keep track of which players are currently on the roster, the league proposed shrinking the offseason to a three-week period in December, instituting weekly rosters, and dropping the amount of times a player can be optioned to the minors during a season from five to four. Between these proposals and the salary cap — to which these proposals are tied — the league believes that their proposal will succeed at “creating more stability in rosters, getting the best players to the Major Leagues more quickly, and accelerating the pace of the offseason.”If you read any of my work from the previous CBA negotiations, when I outlined all the ways that the league’s proposals last time were rooted in attempts to reduce player salaries and increase ownership control over the game, you wouldn’t be surprised to learn that I see the league’s latest pitch to be completely self-serving. By reducing the offseason to a few short weeks in December, the league wants a free agent frenzy like you see in the NFL and NBA…but in truth, the deadline will give teams extra leverage, because, in the words of FanGraphs’ Michael Baumann, “players would be forced to sign before Christmas or risk remaining unemployed until the start of spring training.” Weekly rosters will limit roster turnover, yes, but it will also limit the amount of players who will sit on their team’s version of the Scranton Shuttle, slowly earning service time over the course of the season, increasing team control over bottom-of-the-roster types. And, of course, when all of these are tied to a salary cap, you’re making player contracts and roster spots even more of a zero-sum game than they already are.That being said, there is the core of a good idea here: the inclusion of “quiet periods” in the offseason. At the moment, the Major League Baseball offseason calendar begins immediately after the end of the World Series. The very next day, all players whose contracts have expired become free agents, although they are unable to sign with other teams until the fifth day after the World Series. Practically, this makes this five-day period an exclusive window to re-sign free agents, during which time teams must extend qualifying offers and either accept or reject team options, and players must exercise opt-outs (or not). Oh, and during this time, the trade market opens back up too.Compared to other sports, this is a very short window between the end of the championship and the formal start of the offseason. To put that in perspective, let’s take a look at the timelines that the NFL and NBA use.On February 14, 2027, Super Bowl LXI will be played. The new league year will not begin until almost a month later, on March 9, 2027. In between these two dates, no transactions can officially be completed (while some trades get negotiated and reported on, they cannot officially take place until the start of the new league year), giving teams a period of time after the championship to reflect on the past season and make a plan of action for the offseason.Okay, but the Super Bowl is a one-day affair, so that’s not a perfect one-to-one comparison. What about another sport whose championship can end over a period of time, such as the NBA? Well, the Knicks clinched their first NBA Finals championship on June 13th. The NBA Draft — which is, officially, the last event of the 2025-2026 season, even if everyone thinks of it as the start of the near year — occurred ten days later. The new league year, and thus free agency and the trade market, didn’t open up until July 6th. It’s not quite as much of a breather between the championship and the offseason as the NFL, but it does give more time than we get in baseball.According to Major League Baseball’s pitch, the first five days after the World Series would remain exactly the same, but free agency would not begin until the Winter Meetings in December. On December 21st, free agency would slam shut and a trade moratorium would commence, and neither would open again until the the start of spring training in February. This essentially institutionalizes what already happens on the front end — very few transactions occur during the month of November — guarantees that a lot of business happens at the Winter Meetings (which, with the exception of the Shohei Ohtani sweepstakes, generally happens anyway), and turns January, when the NFL playoffs dominate the sports news cycle, into a dead period. Despite the league’s insistence, this proposal doesn’t exactly transform the offseason; it simply guarantees that it moves at the beat of the league’s drums.If the league genuinely wants to fix the offseason, there’s quite a bit of low-hanging fruit. The current offseason structure is an amalgamation of almost 200 years of evolution, from the player-led amateur clubs of the mid-19th century through today. Free agency begins immediately after the World Series, but the meetings during which their agents are most likely to meet with teams doesn’t occur until six weeks later. Arbitration-eligible players are tendered contracts in November whose values are not known until January. Nobody creating a league from scratch would structure their offseason like this. In fact, the sports videogame franchise that attempts to simulate baseball front offices, , employs its own offseason calendar because the real one is so convoluted that the computer-controlled teams would struggle with it.Ironically, ’s model could supply some inspiration to reform the offseason calendar. When using default settings, players don’t file for free agency until a few weeks after the end of the World Series, which is also the same time as the salary arbitration deadline. This is, of course, done for gameplay considerations, ensuring that both human- and computer-controlled teams know where their budgets stand when free agency begins. The same logic, though, applies to real life. Finishing salary arbitration before free agency opens would give front offices some certainty for embarking on their winter plans, and the fact that it would delay the opening of free agency until, say, late November would turn the Winter Meetings into the free agent marquee event they want it to be, just without the unnatural “hurry up and wait” approach of the league’s proposal. The second “frozen zone” of MLB’s proposal is also, in theory, a good idea — so long as it’s limited to just being a holiday break, not an offseason deadline. The period between Christmas and New Year’s is arguably the quietest part of the baseball calendar, because let’s be honest, everybody wants to spend the holidays with their families, not working. Well, everybody except AJ Preller, apparently. MLB Executive Burner (who is often speculated to be Mike Elias) said in response on Twitter:Even beyond these practical reasons for the delayed start to free agency, it’s also a much more aesthetically pleasing offseason. Think back to the end of the 2024 season. Twenty-four hours after the final out of the World Series, before we even had a chance to think about starting our end-of-season coverage here on Pinstripe Alley, the baseball world had already turned the page and started the offseason. Juan Soto, Alex Verdugo, Anthony Rizzo, Gleyber Torres, and Gerrit Cole (who, you may recall, temporarily exercised his opt-out that winter before the Yankees called his bluff) fell off the active roster and were purged from the Yankees’ website…and that would’ve happened even if the team won. Can you imagine if Mitchell Robinson had gone down the Canyon of Heroes celebrating the Knicks championship while under contract with the Boston Celtics? Theoretically, that’s possible in baseball — highly unlikely, considering cities try not to wait before having their parade, but still possible. And let’s be honest, who really wants to check MLB Trade Rumors while watching their nieces and nephews open up presents from Santa on Christmas morning?Of course, Major League Baseball may have stumbled on some really good ideas, but at the end of the day, do we actually trust that they’ll pursue the good ideas in lieu of chasing a quick buck. With Rob Manfred in charge, the man who — in the words of Keith Law — finds a golden egg and sees only a goose that needs to be killed, I wouldn’t count on it.

item.title: 'I’ve given them 100% of myself' - Chiara Consonni confirms two more years at Canyon-SRAM after victory at Philadelphia Cycling Classic
item.content:encoded: Italian sprinter Chiara Consonni (Canyon-SRAM) had a lot to celebrate Sunday. She earned her second victory of the season at the Philadelphia Cycling Classic and after the race acknowledged she would remain with the team for two more years. "Yes, two more years. For sure there will be a lot of changing in the team with the girls. But I felt the one thing that I never miss in this team is the trust. So I think it's really important as a human, not as only a rider. They give me a lot of trust, so will be a great two more years," she said in Philadelphia after the sprint win.Consonni, who also specialises in endurance disciplines on the track, first signed for the German squad at the beginning of 2025 following her step to Women's WorldTour level with UAE Team ADQ in 2023. Canyon-SRAM confirmed the contract extension on Monday, retaining the 27-year-old until the end of the 2028 season.I decided to extend my contract with CANYON//SRAM because I think I’ve given them 100% of myself, and I believe we can still improve a lot as a team," Consonni said in a team statement. "And the most important thing - because I find people that really believe in me and I want to give them something back."Consonni has won five races on the road since joining Canyon-SRAM; no small feat for a sprinter, in an era that includes a rider as dominant as Lorena Wiebes (Team SD Worx-ProTime). “For me, two years ago, it was really hard to change everything," she explained. "But I feel like many aspects have improved race by race, especially the relationships and the feeling between the girls. I think that if we are a group that really wants to achieve something, we can keep improving, come to the start with the mentality of winning, and then we can do it.”Consonni was a part of the Tour de France Femmes squad which supported Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney to a historic victory on Mont Ventoux - a day which the 27-year-old now holds as her fondest memory within the sport - and then finish on the overall podium in second place.Her extension comes days after the team's first new signing for the 2027 season, as Lidl-Trek's multi-discipline talent Shirin van Anrooij was confirmed to be joining the team. With the expected departure of Niewiadoma-Phinney, securing Consonni's loyalty will be an important step towards determining a new direction for the team heading into the new season.The team's Director of Sport Ralf Aldag expressed his delight over securing two more years of service from the Italian. “Chiara has a great spirit, brings an extra laugh, and always boosts morale. She’s a committed teammate, and always has a really good chance to compete for victories in the sprints. She represents why we all got involved in cycling - being competitive while having fun. "We can unlock more from Chiara if we give her more support, and grow her confidence. Key topic: strengthening the lead-out.”Following the recent Tour of Britain Women, in which Consonni showed strong form by recording two stage podium finishes, she travelled to North America for the revived Philadelphia Cycling Classic, which returned after a 10-year absence, where she was able to translate that strong form into victory."It was a really long season. But yeah, Philadelphia was in my plan from the beginning, and I'm really happy to be here and did this race. And for sure, the winning is always something great," she told media, including , after her win. “I don’t want to try and achieve one particular race result, but I want to try to earn the trust of the girls. I know that I need to give them a lot for them to also give me a lot."Also, I’m just excited to race and to stay with the same people, because now I feel like I’ve found a really nice group and I know everyone much better than I did two years ago. I think that when you know people better, you also understand how to push them, and they know how to do it with me. I want to work with everyone, and keep doing everything that is possible.”Following from her win in Philadelphia, Consonni will race on the road at Grand Prix Stuttgart & Region on September 13 before targeting the UCI Track World Championships in China in October.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to . item.title: Think twice before installing this device promising free movies
item.author: Dan Goodin
item.content:encoded: As online services get better at blocking malicious traffic, the attackers and scammers behind them have been forced to find new ways to reach their targets. The alternative of choice is now what are known as residential proxy networks. These systems funnel millions of home Internet connections into a unified network, and the proxy operators allow attackers to route their malicious traffic through these connections for a fee. The online services see only IP addresses with good reputations and geolocations that don’t stand out.More often than not, the home users have no idea that their connections are being used to facilitate crime and occasionally even nation-state attacks. Users who do know often don’t care much. In exchange for leasing out part of their unlimited bandwidth to others, many get free movie and TV show streaming. Several less tech-savvy people I know who own such digital media players have told me, after I explain how the media players piggyback off their connections, that the bonanza of content is worth it. They find the tangible benefits outweigh the abstract harm they pose.Infecting already compromised devicesResearch published Monday brings the threat into much clearer view. Security firm Plume cataloged a vast ecosystem of malware that preys squarely on users of SuperBox, just one of many media players offering pirated content. These malicious apps can be surreptitiously installed by remote attackers even when the devices are positioned behind a router. While Monday’s deep-dive analysis focused exclusively on SuperBox, Plume warned that dozens of similar streaming devices pose precisely the same threat.

item.title: El Niño is now stronger than at any point in the last 1,000 years, study finds
item.author: Jacek Krywko
item.content:encoded: Every few years, El Niño or its cool counterpart, La Niña, shifts rainfall across the tropics, dries out Australia, floods parts of Peru, and rearranges the weather on most of the planet. The two are the warm and cold swings of a single system, the El Niño–Southern Oscillation, or ENSO, and that system is the largest source of year-to-year climate variation on Earth. Its swings sit atop the steadily rising temperatures driven by global warming.But we didn't know whether global warming was making it stronger. It’s possible that the added energy in the atmosphere and oceans was causing its swings to be more dramatic.“We've been seeing some very strong El Niño events in the late 20th and early 21st century, and what we didn't know was how unusual those are,” said Julie Cole, an environmental scientist at the University of Michigan. Because models disagree with one another and the instrumental data are too short to separate a trend, Cole’s team reconstructed a thousand-year-long ocean surface temperature record by analyzing fossilized Galápagos corals.

item.title: 'Starting to plan for next year will likely be great motivation for Tadej' - Multiple-crash victim Mikel Landa recommends Pogačar look ahead to 2027 after his Vuelta a España abandon
item.content:encoded: As Tadej Pogačar begins his slow recovery process from his major crash in the Vuelta a España, Basque stage racing specialist Mikel Landa recommended that one way that the UAE Team Emirates-XRG leader could try to get over the setback on a mental level was by beginning to plan for 2027.Currently taking part in the Vuelta a España but on his own comeback trail from his latest injuries in a career beset by misfortunes, Landa was only now finding his way back to full form after breaking his pelvis in April in a crash in Itzulia, he told So given his multiple experiences of major injuries, which have seen him abandon the Giro d'Italia in the first week of racing in both 2025 and 2021, as well as the Itzulia Basque Country on several occasions, Landa had considerable first-hand knowledge of how best to handle the recovery process, too. And whilst it remained possible, at least for now, that Pogačar would race again in 2026, Landa felt looking into the mid-term and long-term would also help the Slovenian star get over his dramatic setback."One key thing could be to think about next year a bit and looking ahead. He's still got lots of possible goals," Landa told Cyclingnews on Sunday."This is the first really bad crash he's had, and this isn't an easy sport, even if he's the king of the show."So he needs to have that extra morale boost for sure and starting to plan for next year will likely be a great source of motivation for Tadej."Whilst wishing all the best for Pogačar himself, Landa said he had found it "heartening" that the peloton had collectively slowed down when the Vuelta leader crashed, "to see if there was any way he could get back into the race"."When things like this happen, it brings us together and respect for the rivals is a big part of that," Landa said.Regarding his own recovery from his broken pelvis, Landa began the Vuelta feeling very uncertain of how his form would be, telling reporters he had no idea what he could achieve. However, his motivation was on the rise again as he's "feeling more and more a part of the race and more confident for the last two weeks"."The injury I got from the crash in Itzulia, my fractured pelvis, has sorted itself out now," he explained to . "That was responsible for everything, at first the bones weren't setting properly but now they're no longer giving me any problems.""Right now, it's more a question of lack of form. I've barely raced all year and I'm lacking that race rhythm."Running 47th overall, and a long way out of the fight for the top spots overall, Landa agreed that the absence of Pogačar constituted a major game-changer in the GC hierarchy."The race is really open now and we'll have to see what happens, but I expect there will be a big battle between Mas, Gall and Roglič for the final victory."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to . item.author: Andrew Mearns
item.content:encoded: During my tenure at Pinstripe Alley—hell, during my entire time as a baseball fan—I’ve never been shy about delving into the team’s history and exploring the lives of its long roll call of players, both incredible and regrettable. We provide plenty of other coverage on the current-day activities of the teams, so I like having one spot per day on the schedule to open the ol’ books and tell a story.Whether it’s remembering championship teams, Top 100 players, or notable free agent signings, there’s always something out there to explore. item.title: Google Maps renames "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" even faster than US government
item.author: Ryan Whitwam
item.content:encoded: Trade talks between the US and Canada broke down last week, leading to a wave of tariffs and retaliatory tariffs. US President Donald Trump also fell back on an old favorite to needle his opponents, signing an executive order on Thursday to rename Lake Ontario to "Lake America."The body of water, which straddles the US-Canada border, gave its name to the Canadian province rather than the other way around. Regardless, the US government now refers to this great lake as Lake America—or it will soon. Official US government maps have yet to be updated, but Google wasted no time adopting the new, Trumpian name.Google began rolling out this change for US users on Saturday. The company posted a brief update on its Google Maps blog, noting that it follows the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) for its maps, so the company implies it had no choice but to rename Lake Ontario in Google Maps, which is the most popular mapping platform in the US by a wide margin.

item.title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Claudell Washington
item.author: Kevin Winterhalt
item.content:encoded: Claudell Washington had a darn fine major league career, sticking around for 17 seasons, making a couple of All-Star appearances. More notably, he was part of the World Series champion Oakland Athletics in his rookie season, the third title in a row for the mighty A’s. I can only imagine what that does to the psyche. Unfortunately for Washington, that was his only championship ring.His time as a Yankee accounts for a fraction of his overall career, playing all or part of four seasons in pinstripes. But in a historical quirk, Washington is a surprisingly significant part of Yankee lore.: Claudell Washington: August 31, 1954 (Los Angeles CA): June 10, 2020 (Orinda, CA): 1986-1988, 1990Washington’s career got off to quite the start. As mentioned, the rookie outfielder won a World Series with Oakland in 1974, having just turned 20 years old that August. For his part, though not an everyday starter in the postseason, Washington rose to the moment. He went 7-for-18 in his first taste of playoff baseball.The next season was the finest of his career by almost any metric. He earned his first All-Star Game nod and the As made another trip to the playoffs, though they fell three games to one to Boston. That was the last time Washington played October baseball for a while.After one more season in Oakland, Washington bounced around, playing for Texas, the White Sox, the Mets, and the Braves between 1977 and 1985. Unfortunately for him, he’s perhaps best known during that time for a 1985 arrest for possession of marijuana and cocaine. He did permanently etch his name in baseball lore in 1980, however. Washington notched a three-homer game in 1979 for the White Sox. The next season, he repeated the feat, this time for the Mets. By doing so, he became the third man to accomplish that feat in both leagues, joining Babe Ruth and Johnny Mize.In June 1986, Atlanta dealt him to the Yankees in a trade that saw Ken Griffey, Sr. head to the Braves. Washington re-signed in the Bronx that offseason and was a productive member of the lineup for the next couple years, batting .296/.340/.433 with 39 doubles, 20 homers, 25 stolen bases, and a 111 OPS+ across 228 games.At the old Metrodome in Minnesota on April 20, 1988, Washington hit the 10,000 home run in franchise history, making the Yanks the first club to reach that milestone — no small feat considering how much older plenty of the National League teams are in comparison.That wasn’t his only highlight of the 1988 campaign, either. On September 11th, Washington stepped up to bat against former MVP Willie Hernandez. The Tigers and Yankees endured a marathon in the Bronx, with both sides going scoreless for 10 consecutive innings from the eighth through the 17th. Detroit had finally broken through in the top of the 18th on an RBI single from future Diamondbacks skipper Torey Lovullo.But Hernandez was tired in his third inning of work and walked Rickey Henderson to lead off the home half. That made Rickey the tying run at first base, always a dangerous proposition. Washington was next up though, and he just ended it right then and there. In terms of innings, it was the latest walk-off homer in Yankees history.Washington left New York for the Angels after the 1988 season. If Washington was to be believed, the sticking point was $200,000. He told the :”I was playing with five or six potential Hall of Famers. That’s rare. All I wanted was a $200,000 buyout for an option year and they wouldn’t agree to it. That’s what it was: $200,000.”In the end, he returned to New York, albeit more than a year later. In April 1990, the Angels dealt Washington back to the Yanks, who released him that October after 33 unproductive games for the last-place club. It marked the end of his career.Washington died in June 2020. He had suffered from prostate cancer since 2017.Claudell Washington’s tenure in New York was brief. But he tallied a couple of the more historic homers in franchise history, too. He was also, according to reporter Murray Chass, one of the aforementioned Rickey Henderson’s favorite teammates with the Yankees. Happy heavenly birthday, Claudell Washington!See more of the “Yankees Birthday of the Day” series here.

item.title: Andrea Bagioli moves to XDS-Astana in 2027 as Kazakh team continue busy week on the transfer market
item.content:encoded: Andrea Bagioli transfers to XDS-Astana in 2027 on a two-year deal, marking another move by Alexandr Vinokurov's outfit as part of a productive rebuild for next season. The versatile 27-year-old spent three years at Lidl-Trek. XDS-Astana's transfer activity began with the mid-season signing of Victor Langelotti from Netcompany Ineos. The Monegasque rider jumped into action for the Kazakh team at the Tour of Poland and the Vuelta a España, though he was forced to withdraw from that race on stage 9 due to injuries sustained in a crash. Bagioli's signing follows hot on the heels of Anthony Turgis moving from TotalEnergies, demonstrating Vinokurov's intention to add experience and depth to his squad in the Classics department in particular.“As soon as I learned about XDS Astana Team’s interest and received the offer, I immediately felt that this would be the right choice for me. This is a project I have always followed with interest, and now the opportunity to become part of it really inspires me," Bagioli said. "I know many of my future teammates well, and I have always heard very positive things from them. I think I will be able to quickly integrate into the team and show what I can do over these two seasons. My main goal is to fight for victory whenever the opportunity arises, while also helping the team achieve its important objectives.”The Italian's time at Lidl-Trek has been somewhat disappointing, by contrast with his exploits at the QuickStep organisation prior to his transfer. Bagioli struggled to make an impact at Lidl-Trek, recording just one victory - a stage at this year's Tour of Austria in July. It was the first win for the Italian at the team, ending a period of almost three years without victory. His four years at QuickStep yielded seven wins including one at WorldTour level - a stage of the Volta Catalunya in 2022 - and he will hope to return to his best level in the colours of Astana.General Manager Vinokurov said he has followed the Italian's career for a long time. Now, the 27-year-old Italian is under contract with XDS-Astana through the end of 2028."Andrea started his professional career at a young age, quickly making his mark and achieving a number of impressive results. I believe that at XDS Astana Team, Bagioli will have the opportunity to fulfill his full potential. "Our team performs well in one-day races, which is one of our priority areas, and adding Andrea Bagioli should help us improve our results even further. In addition, he has extensive experience racing Grand Tours, which is always an important factor for us."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to . Images from Chinese rescue teams who have managed to get in by helicopter or hiking show the area has been completely flattened. item.title: Yankees Rivalry Roundup: Tampa wins again; El Gary goes yard for the 200th time
item.author: Kevin Winterhalt
item.content:encoded: After the Yanks bludgeoned Boston Sunday, it was time to scoreboard watch. Most notably, could the Padres do us all a solid and knock off the Rays? To the surprise of absolutely no one, the answer was no. So while the Yankees put more distance between themselves and Boston and clinched the season series between the two eternal rivals, there was no ground gained on Tampa.Elsewhere, a former Baby Bomber achieved a career milestone while a future Hall of Fame hurler further stated his Cooperstown case. Tampa Bay Rays (82-54) 5, San Diego Padres (72-65) 4 (F/11)Bloody Devil Magic. The Padres looked to have this game wrapped up, with a ninth-inning lead and Mason Miller on the mound. Since joining the Padres last season, the All-World closer had surrendered precisely two home runs over 79.2 frames as he took the mound Sunday. So, of course he promptly gave up a game-tying two-run blast to Johnny DeLuca. But hold on. This was no run of the mill home run.As I said, bloody Devil Magic. After a scoreless 10th, the Dads took a lead in the 11th. But it was all for naught. A DeLuca ground ball to Xander Bogaerts ended in an error and re-tied the game. Then, former Yankee farmhand Jorge Mateo ended it with a walk-off single. Chicago White Sox (72-64) 1, Minnesota Twins (65-72) 5: For all intents and purposes, this one was over before the opening frame came to a close. Minnesota plated three in the home first, more than enough for starter Zebby Matthews. Matthews took a shutout into the ninth before the Pale Hose managed to scrape across a run. Matthews’ day ended with 8.1 innings allowing that lone run. That continues a strong run, as he has pitched to a 3.21 ERA in his last seven outings, averaging 6 IP/start.Houston Astros (69-68) 6, New York Mets (61-76) 3: LaMonte Wade, Jr. was Sunday’s hero for Houston. His pinch-hit two-run home run gave the Astros a lead they never surrendered. The victory keeps H-town two games ahead of their intra-state rival Rangers.Texas Rangers (67-70) 7, Milwaukee Brewers (85-52) 4: Texas won Sunday to stay in the mix in the AL West and Wild-Card races. But for Yankees fans, Gary Sánchez was the story. The Kraken clubbed the 200th home run of his career, 138 of which came in pinstripes, in defeat. Sigh. We’ll always have the second half of 2016.Cleveland Guardians (69-68) 11, Kansas City Royals (62-76) 1: Welcome to the José Ramírez Show. The Cleveland third baseman has been mired in his worst offensive season since 2015. Not Sunday, however. Ramírez homered and drove in four as the 3-4-5 batters for Cleveland combined to plate 10 runs.-69) , Athletics (53-) 5: Gunnar Henderson has had a rough 2026. But on Sunday, he looked every bit the young superstar. Four hits, two of which left the yard, led to three runs scored and five batted in as the Os swept the As.Toronto Blue Jays (68-70) 7, Seattle Mariners (64-73) 0: For one day at least, Max Scherzer was “Mad Max” again. While tossing seven frames of one-hit shutout ball, Scherzer punched out 10. The last of those moved him ahead of Gaylord Perry for ninth all-time on the career strikeout list.

item.title: The law won't save us from Meta's 'pervert glasses'. The only solution is mockery | Jonathan Liew
item.author: Jonathan Liew
item.content:encoded: These things are undermining not just our public spaces but the very nature of being human. Let’s shame them off the streetsSo far I am yet to be tempted into purchasing a pair of Ray-Ban Meta glasses. To a certain extent this is a function of possessing a large, misshapen and comically convex head upon which no pair of sunglasses has ever looked remotely appropriate. Nor am I one of those consumers who professes to be “really into gadgets”, a preference I’ve always found weirdly unspecific. It’s subtly telling when people claim to be into “gadgets”, because they’re never talking about, say, a tin opener. What they really mean is something gimmicky and expensive that almost certainly requires the services of a datacentre and enough water to irrigate Kent.And even if I were to surmount these two obstacles, you then get into the ethics of the thing. I’m nobody’s idea of a PR expert, but if your shiny new product keeps requiring patches and updates to prevent people from using it to do degenerate things to women, perhaps it might be worth walking it back to the research and development stage.Jonathan Liew is a Guardian columnistContinue reading...

item.title: 'I haven't looked at the route at all' - Vuelta a España leader Enric Mas admits complete lack of course knowledge for next two weeks
item.content:encoded: Enric Mas may never have led a Grand Tour before last Saturday, but the 31-year-old Spaniard showed no sign of nervousness when he faced the press on Monday with of the Vuelta a España in his possession for the first time. Nor did he seem troubled by the fact that, as he freely admitted, in terms of terrain, he had no idea what challenges await him in the remaining 12 stages in this year's Vuelta.However, if Mas does lack precise race knowledge of this year's route, overall it's all but impossible for too many surprises. In his 10 years of racing and eight Vuelta a España appearances, Mas has finished four times on the podium of the Vuelta, but never in the top three of any other Grand Tour. True to his consistently good form in the Vuelta, he was running second overall when Tadej Pogačar crashed out of the race on Saturday, and duly 'inherited' the lead, for the first time in his career in any Grand Tour. Thanks to Mas, Movistar - historically one of the most successful stage racing teams - have found themselves at the centre of a GC battle for the first time since Mas finished third in the Vuelta back in 2024. It also represents a major step back into the GC arena for the rider from Mallorca, who suffered a series of injuries since July 2025, and whose participation in the Giro d'Italia, his first ever, this May, came nowhere near producing the desired results."Recently I've been through some difficult times, but they've not been the worst of my career," Mas said on his rest day press conference on Monday, in comments reported by Spanish news agency ."There are far worse things than a heavy fall or certain physical problems. It's true I've had a tough time of getting out of that situation and regaining form, but I'm happy to be where I am, with the form I have, and to be smiling again in La Vuelta."Mas said he has not changed anything in particular to hit his current high level of form, although he did miss the Tour de France this summer for the first time since 2018. Nor did he feel any different after having tracked down Pogačar on the stage to Castelló after the Slovenian had attacked."I'm the same Enric as ever, although it's true that this was a moment that gave me a lot of confidence."At the same time, he admitted that he doesn't have a clue abut what stages are left in this year's race: in more ways than one then, given his lack of experience at leading a Grand Tour, the next two weeks for Mas will be a voyage in the dark."Shall I tell you the truth [about the upcoming route]? I don't have the slightest idea about it. We still haven't done the team meeting," Mas said."There are some stages which I know will be crucial for the overall, but in the last two days I haven't had time for anything, I haven't looked at anything." While normally before a race begins, he'll work out a general plan, Mas said, "This time round, I haven't looked [at the route] at all."Mas' overall advantage is a slender one, with a 1:18 gap on Roglič, whilst Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) is at 1:39. While Gall recently took his first Grand Tour podium in the Giro d'Italia, Roglič has four Vueltas to his name, two of them - 2021 and 2024 - ahead of Mas. He also finished third in 2023, three places ahead of Mas."I think given his history in the Vuelta, Roglič is the rider who most worries me regarding [the overall victory in Granada]," Mas said. However, he denied that he was scared of trying to win it, whilst trying not to grow obsessed with the idea that for the first time in his ten year career, he was in the best position ever to do precisely that - and conquer the Vuelta at last. "It's not a question of fear. It's just that if I spend the whole day thinking about it, finally it ends up being a stress-fest which I don't need to have right now," he said."I just want to enjoy this moment, enjoy wearing red, enjoy being with the team and we have to concentrate on what's coming up, too. And that's pretty much it."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to . The flyby by two Embraer jets, operated by the local airline Airlink, happened on Saturday before the second rugby union Test between South Africa and New Zealand in Cape Town.The flight tracking service Flightradar24 estimated that the lead jet passed just 41-46 feet (12-14 metres) above the roof of Cape Town Stadium, with the crowd and the world’s top-ranked rugby teams below. item.title: ChatGPT and Reddit now face EU's toughest online safety rules
item.author: Barbara Moens, Financial Times
item.content:encoded: OpenAI’s ChatGPT will have to comply with tougher EU rules such as removing illegal content or face potential fines, the European Commission said on Monday, as Brussels grapples with how its existing digital regulation applies to rapidly evolving AI services.The Commission said the chatbot, social media forum Reddit, and gaming platform Roblox would be classified as so-called very large online platforms under the EU Digital Services Act, its landmark online safety regime.The designation means all three services will face additional obligations such as removing illegal content and protecting the privacy and security of minors and could face fines of up to 6 percent of their global revenue if they fail to comply.

item.title: Tadej Pogačar set for 'serious operation' in next two days as UAE team boss says it 'doesn't seem easy' to recover in time for World Championships
item.content:encoded: UAE Team Emirates-XRG team principal Mauro Gianetti has detailed the road ahead for Tadej Pogačar as he begins his recovery from the crash that ended his Vuelta a España on Saturday. Pogačar has posted on Instagram since his accident, putting on a brave face from his hospital bed in Barcelona, where he remains this week as he awaits surgery. According to Gianetti, his collarbone can only be operated on when his concussions symptoms subside."We must now wait for the concussion to go dow. Probably on Tuesday, if all goes well, he can have surgery on his collarbone," Gianetti said on the Bartoli Time show on the French radio station RMC Sport."The collarbone fracture is displaced so it will be a fairly big operation. It will be possible on Tuesday or Wednesday depending on his recovery from the concussion."Pogačar had been leading the only Grand Tour yet to be added to his glittering palmarès from the opening stage in his home region of Monaco, and had won 50% of the six completed stages. His shot at Grand Tour history has now gone up in smoke and now, as the rest of the season goes, there is understandably major doubt."It's still quite early to say," Gianetti answered, when asked whether or not the reigning world champion would be able to line up in Montréal to defend his title at the end of September. "We tried to avoid the discussion, because it's not the right time to make decisions. First of all, we have to see the recovery and how the operation goes on Tuesday or Wednesday. From there, we will have a slightly clearer framework to know if he has time to return for the end of the season or not."We will be able to approach this with a little more calmness and with Tadej who will have at least recovered from the concussion. It's not the time to make decisions with emotion; we'll have to wait a few days."The end of the season includes not only the possibility to triple up on the road race world title he has won two years running, but also the opportunity to extend his record of five consecutive victories at the fifth and final Monument of the season, Il Lombardia. Gianetti was quick to temper any expectation about Pogačar's potential appearance at the World Championships road race, in Montréal which is now less than a month away. "Yes, the time is very short, he is still in the hospital, he has not been operated on. Of course, it doesn't seem easy to recover for the World Championship," Gianetti said. "But hey, we'll see a little bit with the evolution in the next few days. The fracture of the collarbone is quite bad, because it requires a fairly serious operation and therefore it doesn't help."Gianetti's fears for PogačarGianetti also opened up on his fears for Pogačar following the dramatic crash on Saturday."I was very scared, because when you see the riders who have crashed, you know that the speeds are so high that every time they fall, they hurt themselves." He went on to express relief at seeing the Slovenian get up and try to continue. "When I saw that he got up and wanted to start racing again, I was a little relieved. I said to myself: 'Ok he's standing, he's walking and he wants to continue'. In the end it was clear that he couldn't. But we were scared."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to . item.title: NASA's next "great observatory" begins mission to widen our view of the Universe
item.author: Stephen Clark
item.content:encoded: NASA's $4.3 billion Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, equipped with a 300-megapixel camera sighted through a refurbished spy mirror, launched Sunday from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on a mission to reveal the mysterious forces driving the Universe.Unlike Webb, which suffered many years of delays before reaching space, Roman arrived at the launch pad nine months before NASA's commitment to send it skyward by May 2027.
