item.title: UCI Mountain Bike World Championships: Tom Pidcock solos to elite men's Olympic cross-country world title
item.content:encoded: Britain’s Tom Pidcock surged from the fifth row of the grid to win the elite men’s title at the UCI Mountain Bike World Championships at Vale di Sole in Italy on Sunday. It was the second rainbow jersey for the two-time Olympic champion after his 2023 world title in Scotland.Pidcock powered away from compatriot Charlie Aldridge on the penultimate lap to take the victory, crossing the line 17 seconds ahead of second place. Canada’s Cole Punchard took third 31 seconds behind the winner.Mathieu van der Poel, who also started on the fifth row, finished 4:40 back in 30th place, leaving the Dutch rider to continue chasing the one rainbow jersey missing from his palmares.An emotional Pidcock dedicated his victory to 19-year-old Finlay Tarling, who died after an accident at the Volta a Portugal on August 14th.“I don't have much words. It was a hard road here after the Tour [de France], to be honest. I want to dedicate this win to Finlay Tarling, to Josh. I mean, seeing [Josh] start of the Vuelta [a España] was pretty incredible. So I want to dedicate him and his family.”“I knew there was a course that you really couldn't overpace yourself, and you had to ride within your limit. And I crashed pretty bad in practice on Friday, and my back was hurting from the first lap. I really couldn't go any harder, so I'm lucky that the pace I could hold was good enough to get to the front, and then last two laps I had to push whatever I could and see if I could try and stretch that gap before a final sprint. Yeah that was a pretty hard race.”The French riders came out strong from the gun, pushing the pace and quickly creating a split at the front, wanting to distance Pidcock and Van der Poel. They had a reason to be worried as one of them, Pidcock, was chasing hard, finally connecting with the front halfway through the eight-lap race. After some yoyoing, the Brit made his way to the front on the sixth lap and started to apply pressure on the group, which included Aldridge, Punchard, Adrien Boichis (France), and Martin Vidaurre (Chile). One by one, riders fell off the pace, with only Aldridge able to keep pace until he was finally also dropped.Tom Pidcock (GBr) Great BritainCharlie Aldridge (GBr) Great BritainCole Punchard (Can) item.title: The datacenter backlash is bringing the entire political spectrum together – against big tech billionaires
item.author: Aaron Regunberg
item.content:encoded: The movement against datacenters is uniting Americans because they perfectly illustrate how a few individuals hold all the power to control decisions that affect our livesBryce Gustafson has been knocking on doors in Indiana for more than a decade. The lead organizer with Citizens Action Coalition (CAC), a consumer and environmental organization, he usually encounters a mix of reactions when he’s out canvassing; whatever issue he’s talking about, there’s always at least a few people on the other side. But at a recent festival in the rural town of Monrovia, Indiana, he was struck by an unusual spirit of unity.He was there about a proposed datacenter, a 550-acre (222-hectare) Google project in this small town of 1,600 people. “I had 50 people I talked to,” Gustafson told me. “Nobody wanted that datacenter in their community. And at least a half a dozen people came up to me to say, ‘Hey, I voted for Trump. What the heck’s he doing, supporting these things?’”Continue reading...

Philadelphia Cycling Classic Women: Chiara Consonni victorious in first edition since 2016
item.author: laura@cyclingnews.com (Laura Weislo)
item.content:encoded: Chiara Consonni (Canyon-SRAM) scored an emphatic victory in the revived Philadelphia Cycling Classic, out-sprinting Alexandra Volstad (EF Education-Oatly) and Ella Sabo (Virginia's Blue Ridge TWENTY28).The Italian narrowly edged out the young Canadian with a bike throw after a crash disrupted the final kilometre of the 101.9km race.When asked how it felt to take her first win on US soil, Consonni said, "Really, really nice! You know, it was a really long travel, and it's not easy with the jet lag to arrive here and do a race like this."Consonni stayed patient amid numerous attacks on the hilly final circuits, waiting as EF Education-Oatly and her own team tried repeatedly to break up the peloton, before hitting out late in the final 200 metres."We knew that the climb can make a difference, and we managed quite good. The last time we tried to attack to split a bit of the group, but then in the end we re-grouped together."I think we were in numbers in the end, so we also managed really good the last two small laps with the breakaway. Then the girls made a really good job for me for the lead-out, and I only did my sprint, and we achieved the first place. I need to say thanks to them."Volstad was philosophical after coming within a tyre's width of her first pro win."It's pretty nice. We've been learning all year as a team, doing the sprints together and stuff," she said."And I think like lately we've been getting a lot of podiums, so I think it's starting to come together with our young team. So I'd say I'm pretty happy, and I love the racing in the US, so it's a cherry on top."The first running of the Philadelphia Cycling Classic began under a cloudy sky with a crash at the back of the 116-rider peloton keeping the race neutral for the run-out along Kelly Drive to allow the affected riders to rejoin. Once racing got underway, EF Education-Oatly announced their intentions by controlling the pace on the first trip up the Manayunk Wall - the famous short but steep ascent.Auke De Buysser led the peloton over the summit, as the steady pace caused a bit of damage at the tail end of the bunch. Sofia Arreola (Virginia's Blue Ridge TWENTY28) claimed the mountains points on Lemon Hill – the smaller of the climbs on the 23.2km circuit – but the race remained together until the start of the second lap.Mairen Lawson (Aegis) and Farah-Dale Morris (Automatic Racing) made a move and gained 20 seconds, but they were caught on the Manayunk Wall. EF Education-Oatly led again on the Manayunk Wall with Babette van der Wolf leading over the top, while Elizabeth Dicon (HigherDose | Renova) took the points on Lemon Hill before a breakaway could be established.Elisa Valtulini (Vini-Fantini-BePink) attacked on lap 3 to form the longest breakaway of the race. She was joined by Haixin Dong (XDS China), Rachel Galler (1K Flips-FTP Racing Jakroo), Philadelphia local Kim Stoveld (Automatic Racing), Marlen Lawson (Aegis x Leaders of Enchantment), Galen Bolard (Competitive Edge), and Rebecca Lang (Winston Salem-Flow). They gained 40 seconds before the wall, with Bolard riding away on the steepest section.Bolard claimed the points, heading down with 25 seconds as EF Education-Oatly continued to control the reduced peloton. The breakaway came back together minus Dong and re-established a 40-second lead as they headed in for their last long lap. Bolard won the sprint on Lemon Hill, too, with Lawson distanced, and then Galler lost contact, too.EF Education-Oatly swept past the breakaway at the base of the wall, pulling away another breakaway of five, with Kristen Faulkner and Van der Wolf (EF Education-Oatly), Agnieszka Skalniak-Sojka and Chiara Consonni (Canyon-SRAM) followed by the last winner of the race in 2016, Megan Guarnier (CCB Kenetik p/b Levine Law Group).They began the descent with ten seconds on a further-reduced chasing group of around 20 riders but faced three ascents of Lemon Hill after the flat run down Kelly Drive and 21.5km to go.With two of the WorldTour teams represented, Human Powered Health were forced to do much of the chasing, and the breakaway was reeled in with roughly 10km to go.There were several attacks on the short laps, with Aegis and Vini Fantini putting in short-lived digs. EF Education-Oatly and Canyon-SRAM were aggressive in the final kilometres, but the race came back together for the bunch sprint.Chiara Consonni (Ita) Canyon-SRAM zondacryptoAlexandra Volstad (Can) EF Education-OatlyElla Sabo (USA) Virginia'S Blue Ridge Twenty28Kristen Faulkner (USA) EF Education-OatlyMarit Raaijmakers (Ned) Human Powered HealthAgnieszka Skalniak-Sójka (Pol) Canyon-SRAM zondacryptoGiada Borghesi (Ita) Human Powered HealthJamie Chapman Vini Fantini- BepinkGaia Segato (Ita) Vini Fantini- BepinkMegan Guarnier CCB p/b Levine Law GroupGalen Bolard Competitive Edge RacingMinke Solbjørk Anderson (Den) EF Education-OatlySofia Arici (Ita) Vini Fantini- BepinkAndrea Cyr HigherDOSE | RenovaBabette Van Der Wolf (Ned) EF Education-OatlyLauren Stephens Aegis x Leaders of EnchantmentTiffany Cromwell (Aus) Canyon-SRAM zondacryptoMaike Van Der Duin (Ned) Canyon-SRAM zondacryptoSkylar Schneider Fearless Femme p/b The BeasleyAlexis Magner (USA) EF Education-OatlyRebecca Lang Team Winston Salem - item.title: Vuelta a España: Race leader Enric Mas outsprints Oscar Onley to win stage 9 on Alto de Aitana
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Enric Mas (Movistar) scored a statement stage victory at the Vuelta a España, outsprinting Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) in a two-man dash to the line to score his first win in four years atop the Alto de Aitana on stage 9.The Spaniard, racing his first day in the leader's red jersey, proved the strongest man of the GC group, attacking 3.2km from the finish of the arduous 187km stage and taking Onley with him.He led from the front in the final kilometre, duly dispatching the Briton in the closing sprint as Primož Roglič (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) rounded out the podium, 12 seconds down."Now I understand Tadej. The jersey gives you wings," Mas joked after the stage, reported ."From yesterday afternoon until now, I think the team has done a perfect job. We've been incredibly calm the whole time and controlled the situation very well."I've been excited like a little kid since the start, and to be able to win with the jersey, I assure you, is a very, very special feeling."The race up the Aitana featured a long set-up ride by Decathlon CMA CGM, the French team pushing a high pace to launch Felix Gall's assault on the red jersey. The Austrian made his move 7km from the line, going time and again, but he couldn't get any separation from his rivals.Instead, it was new race leader Mas who made the difference. He matched every move by Gall before making one of his own. Surprisingly, Gall couldn't match the acceleration and quickly shed time in the race to the top.Onley went along for the ride as Mas pushed on at the front, while Roglič attempted to bridge across but couldn't quite do it. Gall was further back, losing time rather than making it up.The result leaves Mas with an extended lead in the general classification, 1:18 up on Roglič. Gall remains in third place, 1:39 off the lead, while Onley is up to fourth overall, 2:20 down.The Vuelta a España continued without former leader Tadej Pogačar on stage 9, with 5,000 metres of elevation – more than any other stage – across six climbs and a summit finish at the Alto de Aitana on the menu.There were few flat metres during the 187.4km stage and the Puerto de Tárbena (7.2km at 5.4%), Puerto de El Miserat (5.2km at 10%), Puerto de Tollos (4.1km at 5.8%), Puerto de Tudons (7km at 5.3%), and Puerto de Benifallim (4.8km at 5.8%) lay on the route ahead of the summit finish (22km at 5.8%), visited for the first time in a decade.Attacks flew from the start of the day, including the likes of Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), Alexey Lutsenko (NSN), Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious), and Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility).Pavel Sivakov was also off the front, part of UAE Team Emirates-XRG's recalibrated strategy of aggression. At the top of the Puerto de Tárbena, he, Lutsenko and Kron were joined by Alastair Mackellar (EF Education-EasyPost) and Alessandro Romele (XDS-Astana) in the move.There was more attacking behind, though, and gaps remained small, even 40km into the stage. Only 45 seconds separated the leading quintet and the peloton as a larger chase group raced between them.UAE Team Emirates-XRG pair Kevin Vermaerke and Finn Fisher-Black were in the chase, as was Buitrago, Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech), Embret Svestad-Bårdseng (Netcompany Ineos), Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal-QuickStep), Urko Berrade (Kern Pharma), Bruno Armirail (Visma-Lease a Bike), Gijs Leemreize (Picnic-PostNL), and Stefan Küng (Tudor).The chasers bridged the gap to make it 15 up front after 55km of racing, before hitting the steep inclines of the Puerto de Miserat.On the road to the Miserat, a group of 12 clipped off the front to try and chase, with Cort, Raúl Garcia Pierna (Movistar), and Filippo Zana (Soudal-QuickStep), Gianni Vermeersch (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), Walter Calzoni, Marcel Camprubí, Milan Vader (Pinarello-Q36.5), Atilla Valter (Bahrain Victorious), Pau Martí (NSN), Sylavin Moniquet (Cofidis), José Manuel Díaz (Burgos-Burpellet-BH), and Oliver Peace (Picnic-PostNL) among their number.Further back, the peloton was led by Movistar on behalf of new race leader Enric Mas, the Spanish squad letting the breakaway riders take a three-minute lead.The two breakaway groups merged after the Puerto de El Miserat, with the new-look break holding a near five-minute lead heading into the final 100km. Buitrago, with the polka dot jersey in his sights, led the race over the Miserat and the Puerto de Tollos, adding 13 points to his tally and taking the virtual classification lead.Movistar continued to set the pace on the front behind as Buitrago added another three KOM points over the next climb of the Tudons before several riders, led by Romele, attacked off the front in the valley road afterwards.It was Romele who led the race over the Puerto de Benifallim, 30 seconds up on lead chaser Camprubí. Six minutes down the climb, Decathlon CMA CGM took over from Movistar in the peloton for their leader Felix Gall.On the descent, Sivakov joined Camprubí in chasing down Romele, joining him partway down the run towards the base of the Aitana. The trio headed into the final 40km of the race with a 50-second advantage over the strongest of the chasers, including Vermaerke, Paret-Peintre, Debruyne, Buitrago, Vader, Zana, and Kron.The leading trio hit the Aitana with 1:20 over the rest as Decathlon continued their work in the peloton, hitting the climb with a five-minute deficit. The first move of the climb came from Vader, Buitrago, Paret-Peintre, and Zana, who jumped clear of the chasers, passing a dropped Romele.Jordan Labrosse ended his mega-turn for Decathlon with 14km to run, leaving five of his Decathlon teammates at the head of the GC group just 3:30 off the leaders. Callum Scotson's turn took another 1:30 off the gap, while Léo Bisiaux and Matthew Riccitello also assisted the pacemaking before Gregor Mühlberger took over with Gall in his wheel.Just inside 10km to go, Sivakov saw a chance to go clear and took it, leaving Camprubí behind. His time in the lead was numbered, too, though, and he looked certain to be caught. Mühlberger almost sprinted to the 7km mark before Gall made his move, a minute behind Sivakov.The Austrian had Mas and a host of other GC contenders on his wheel, and the group swelled as the pace soon slowed. He went again at 6km to go, this time with Widar leading the chase, before, once again, the big names went along.Carapaz was next to make a move, accelerating clear 5.5km from the finish. The Ecuadorian briefly got clear before there was a regrouping a kilometre later, the favourites – plus a resurgent Buitrago – catching and passing Sivakov.Gall went again at 3.8km to go, and again was unable to break free. Mas, having matched each previous move, was next up, going at 3.2km to go and taking Onley with him. Roglič was next on the road, almost coming across under the 2km banner while Gall had nothing left to give.Gall languished 35 seconds down and counting as the Mas hit the final kilometre. Roglič couldn't match the pace, either, leaving the race for the win up to Mas and Onley in a two-up sprint. It was Mas who led it out with Onley behind, and he held the front all the way to the line to celebrate victory in red at the Vuelta a España.Enric Mas Nicolau (Spa) Movistar TeamOscar Onley (GBr) item.title: Bretagne Classic: Alex Aranburu takes WorldTour victory for Cofidis after decisive attack in final kilometres
item.content:encoded: In a dynamic and aggressive race, Alex Aranburu put in a decisive attack just inside the final 2km of the race to win the Bretagne Classic CIC in Plouay. The Cofidis rider jumped from a lead front group that formed after the breakaway was caught with six kilometres to go.Alexander Kamp (Uno-X Mobility) gave chase solo but was not able to catch the Spaniard and took second, crossing the line four seconds later. Alessandro Borgo (Bahrain Victorious) was third, from the 11-rider front group.“I’m super happy, it’s a great team victory. All my teammates were particularly valuable, like Benjamin Thomas who got into the breakaway," Aranburu said in a team release."Towards the end, I knew it wasn’t going to be easy and that I had to be especially focused. I tried to stay calm and give it my all. I’m very proud to be part of this incredible week for Cofidis. It’s definitely one of the best victories of my career.”After being kept on a leash of around a three-minute gap by Alpecin-Premier Tech, the early breakaway reformed as the riders tackled the three finishing circuits, while behind the Visma-Lease a Bike squad attacked multiple times but were not able to get away.The numerous accelerations on the undulating course led to splits and chaos in the field as often happens in this race until ultimately the last breakaway rider was caught.A select group of 11 riders sped away at the front. It included Aranburu and his teammate Dylan Teuns, Emil Herzog (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), Paul Lapeira (Decathlon CMA CGM) and Romain Grégoire (Groupama-FDJ United). With three kilometres to go, they had 16 seconds on the chasing field.French star Paul Magnier (Soudal-Quickstep) went down in a multi-rider crash with 50 kilometres to go and abandoned the race.For its 95th edition, the Bretagne Classic reshaped its route, cutting 34 kilometres to 228.3km while retaining a demanding 3,663 metres of elevation gain on a rolling route centred around Plouay in Brittany. The race began with a 143km clockwise large loop north through Gouraec, Pontivy, Le Sourn and Saint-Barthélemy, leading to a 35km anti-clockwise loop before returning to Plouay for three 16.6km finishing circuits.The finale brought several familiar challenges, including the return of the Ty Marrec climb, absent from the race since 2019. A succession of short climbs and descents followed, with the Rostervel ascent coming with nine kilometres to go. Five kilometres later, the riders faced the Côte de Lezot climb before the final push towards Kerscoulic and the finish.Under cloudy skies, with intermittent rain, the early breakaway was initiated by Sjoerd Bax (Pinarello Q36.5), and he was soon joined by Markus Hoelgaard (Uno-X Mobility) and Alexy Faure Prost (Picnic PostNL). The trio built up a gap of over three minutes in the first half of the race.With 91 kilometres,, two riders, Baptiste Veistroffer (Lotto-Intermarché) and Emil Herzog (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), bridged up, making it five off the front as the gap was down to 1:10 to the Alpecin-Premier Tech-led peloton.The extra firepower increased the gap to 1:30, which was helped by a crash in the pack taking down a few riders with 86km to go.Once the gap went down to under to one-minute mark with 63 km to go, Per Strand Hagenes (Visma-Lease a Bike) attacked as Decathlon CMA CGM was taking over the pacemaking on a climb. The accelerations caused a momentary split in the pack, and reduced the gap, leading to three riders jumping across the 24-second gap, and a chase group formed as the riders sped towards the end of the medium loop.Visma continued to attack off the front, with more splits and reshuffling at the front as another crash took down multiple riders, including Paul Magnier (Soudal-Quickstep) with 50 km to go. After trying to continue, the French star put his bike down and walked into an ambulance. The reformed break included Bax, Faure Prost, Hoelgaard, Herzog, Quinten Hermans (Pinarello Q36.5), Liam Slock (Lotto-Intermarché) and Benjamin Thomas (Cofidis). Though Bax and Faure Prost would fall off the pace, leaving five riders off the front.Crossing the finish line for the first time, seeing three laps to go, the six-rider break had 25 seconds on a first chase group with Tim Rex (Visma-Lease a Bike) and AJ August (Netcompany Ineos), and 41 seconds on the second chase, with the peloton further back after the crash.The break still had 54 seconds on the 10-rider chase group that August tried to whittle down on the Ty Marrec climb and 1:24 on the peloton led by Alpecin-Premier Tech.A lack of cooperation in the chase group slowed down their effort to catch the break, as NSN and EF Education-EasyPost put riders in the rotation in the peloton with 25km to go. Along with August and Rex, the chase group included Ewen Costiou (Groupama-FDJ United) and Robert Stannard (Bahrain Victorious).With 22km to go, Visma’s Victor Campenaerts and Louis Barré attacked at the front of the peloton after they had caught the chase group, but though the accelerations stretched out the field, it all stayed together.The breakaway of five of Slock, Herzog, Hoelgaard, Hermans, and Thomas had a 57-second gap as they started the third and final lap with 16.6km to go.Attacks flew at the front of the peloton on a climb, with TotalEnergies’ Alexandre Delettre trying to launch Mathieu Burgaudeau, and Barré continuing his aggressive racing as the group formed and reformed.Inside of six kilometres to go, the break was caught on a climb, as more riders tried to escape, causing another split at the front. item.content:encoded: Deal that will reportedly see US take control of 65bn barrels of Venezuelan oil has provoked outrage in her countryVenezuela’s interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, has defended her government’s highly controversial energy deal with Donald Trump, insisting the South American country will maintain ownership and sovereignty over its massive oil reserves.Rodríguez, who assumed power in January after Trump ordered the abduction of the president, Nicolás Maduro, took to the airwaves on Saturday to push back against criticism of what the US president has called “the biggest oil deal in world history”.Continue reading...

Starting second on the grid, the Ducati rider passed polesitter Bezzecchi on lap 7 of 23 and then fended off a challenge from KTM rival Acosta to secure his fourth win of the season.Aprilia’s Bezzecchi had no ...Keep reading

item.title: Marquez slashes Martin's MotoGP lead with Aragon win
item.author: Valentin Khorounzhiy
item.content:encoded: Marc Marquez was victorious in MotoGP's 2026 Aragon Grand Prix, taking home full points for his title defence.Marquez faced a spirited challenge at the left-hander-dominated circuit, one of his MotoGP favourites - but ultimately took a relatively comfortable win.The source of that challenge was a surprise, for it wasn't poleman Marco Bezzecchi but KTM rider Pedro Acosta, still chasing his first grand prix win.Bezzecchi led off pole but was again lunged by Marquez at Turn 1. Marquez looked to have completed the move like on Saturday, but this time was very slow through Turns 2 and 3 with what looked like a stuck ride height device - allowing not just Bezzecchi back past, but Jorge Martin through as well.But Marquez forced his way past Martin through the Turn 15 left-hander (with Acosta also sneaking through), then set about catching Bezzecchi back up.He made his move at the same Turn 15 corner on lap six, then squeezing Bezzecchi to the inside of the track on the back straight - and as they braked into Turn 16, Bezzecchi didn't just yield to Marquez but lost second to a sudden round-the-outside dart from Acosta.The KTM man, who will be Marquez's team-mate at Ducati next year, hounded Marquez over the next few laps, before a string of 1m46s laps from Marquez finished the fight.He spent the rest of the race managing his advantage over Acosta, which was ultimately in little doubt despite a couple of minor mistakes from Marquez.Bezzecchi completed the podium, followed by Alex Marquez and championship leader Martin. Martin, thus, leaves Aragon with 19 points in hand over Marquez - and 24 over Bezzecchi.Ducati riders Fermin Aldeguer and Fabio Di Giannantonio rounded out the top seven, Aldeguer having worked his way past Di Giannantonio. The other two Ducati men, Pecco Bagnaia and Franco Morbidelli, exited the grand prix in early crashes from the top 10.Diogo Moreira kept a train of riders behind his LCR-run Honda for most of the grand prix, ultimately settling for ninth as he yielded to Enea Bastianini on the final lap.Jack Miller was the top Yamaha runner again, in 11th, just behind KTM's Brad Binder. Miller's Pramac team-mate Toprak Razgatlioglu was the third rider to crash out of the race.The only other DNF was that of Trackhouse Aprilia's Raul Fernandez, who had an apparent gearbox failure early on.1 Marc Marquez (Ducati)2 Pedro Acosta (KTM) +1.754s3 Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia) +3.629s4 Alex Marquez (Gresini Ducati) +8.687s5 Jorge Martin (Aprilia) +12.572s6 Fermin Aldeguer (Gresini Ducati) +17.687s7 Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Ducati) +23.136s8 Enea Bastianini (Tech3 KTM) +25.741s9 Diogo Moreira (LCR Honda) +25.899s10 Brad Binder (KTM) +26.441s11 Jack Miller (Pramac Yamaha) +27.206s12 Joan Mir (Honda) +27.999s13 Alex Rins (Yamaha) +28.276s14 Luca Marini (Honda) +29.794s15 Johann Zarco (LCR Honda) +30.003s16 Pol Espargaro (Tech3 KTM) +35.874s17 Lorenzo Savadori (Trackhouse Aprilia) +49.761s18 Fabio Quartararo (Yamaha) +51.657sDNF Toprak Razgatlioglu (Pramac Yamaha)DNF Raul Fernandez (Trackhouse Aprilia) DNF Pecco Bagnaia (Ducati)DNF Franco Morbidelli (VR46 Ducati)

item.title: Watch the Philadelphia Cycling Classic live on Cyclingnews
item.author: laura@cyclingnews.com (Laura Weislo)
item.content:encoded: The Philadelphia Cycling Classic returns after a decade off the North American calendar and is on the ground for the refreshed edition.Watch the elite women's race from 8:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. EDT and the men's from noon until approximately 4:45 p.m. EDT.US champion Quinn Simmons (Lidl-Trek) and Olympic champion Kristen Faulkner (EF Education-Oatly) headline the start lists.'Philly' was one of the most important races in North America from 1984 until its demise in 2016, serving as the US Pro National Championships for men until USA Cycling created a standalone event in 2006.The Philadelphia Cycling Classic course runs from Logan Circle along Kelly Drive and the Schuylkill River to the 'Manayunk Wall' - a short but very steep climb kicking up to 16% gradients - before returning via the shorter Lemon Hill.It's the same route that produced famous champions like Eric Heiden, Petra Rossner, Ina Teutenberg, André Greipel, the only men's two-time winner Kiel Reijnen and, in ancient times, Lance Armstrong. will have full coverage from the men's and women's races.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: ‘Without us, no wheel would turn’: the unsung heroes keeping England’s transport moving
item.author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
item.content:encoded: On shift, but out of sight – from ‘that person with the table tennis bats’ on the airport tarmac to remote signallers managing rail trafficNot many people get to park their car here – bang in the middle of Heathrow airport, on the taxiway just a stretch of grass away from where a line of passenger planes is coming in to land.It’s close enough to see the shimmering air and smoke as nose tyres hit the tarmac. “An A380 will put down as much rubber as a car’s entire tyre,” Jack Quantick-Thorne says. He knows – part of his job is to ensure the runway team scrapes it off and patches things up overnight. And it is all recycled, he adds.Continue reading...

item.title: 'Everything is possible' – Felix Gall says it's a new start for the Vuelta a España following Tadej Pogačar's abandon
item.content:encoded: The first full day of the 2026 Vuelta a España without former leader Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) sees the GC battle return to a much more wide-open phase, according to one of the key contenders, Felix Gall.The 2026 Giro d'Italia runner-up and winner of the Vuelta a Burgos in August – one of the key warm-up races for the Vuelta a España together with the Tour de Pologne - Gall was always considered a contender for GC, something he's confirmed in the first week of racing. Following Pogačar's untimely exit, Gall is currently running third overall behind Enric Mas (Movistar) and Primož Roglič (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), 1:11 behind the Spaniard.Before Pogačars's abandon, Gall had ruled himself out of the battle for the overall victory, with his team putting in some of the strongest performances to date in the Vuelta in the mountains, even dislodging UAE – but not Pogačar himself – from the front positions on the first crunch mountain stage through Andorra.Speaking at the start of the next big mountain stage, to Aitana, Gall began his mixed zone interview with and other reporters by wishing Pogačar the best of luck and a speedy recovery. But at the Vuelta, he said, without the Slovenian competing, "a new race begins""With Tadej crashing, it was quite a shock, felt pretty unreal yesterday," Gall said."I wish him all the best, hopefully he'll soon be back. But that's part of cycling; today it means we have a new race now, everything is possible."For a few riders there are some big opportunities, also stage wins. It's a long, hard day; we will see how the teams react, but for now it's a new start to the race."Gall said that although Decathlon would do some work on the front if needed, but noted it was up to Movistar, as race leaders, to keep control of events.As for whether Gall could take his first ever Grand Tour victory in Granada, the Austrian climber and Tour de France stage winner said "Maybe it's possible now, but we're not even in week 2."Today is the queen stage, I would almost say, next to Granada, and it's certainly a key GC stage. People will want to win the stage, and there will be a big fight for the breakaway, too. Everything is possible."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: UCI Mountain Bike World Championships: Nael Rouffiac wins men's U23 XCO race with attack two laps out from line
item.author: simone.giuliani@futurenet.com (Simone Giuliani)
item.content:encoded: After 1:17:20 of racing the 20-year-old French rider clinched the rainbow jersey with a nine second gap to his compatriot Alix Andre Gallis. At 13 seconds back it was Swiss rider Nicolas Halter in third, who won the short-track."I am speechless. It is a dream come true," said Rouffiac. "The plan was to attack towards the end, but I was feeling good and decided to go for it on the fifth lap. I am really happy to share this with a teammate. It was the perfect day."It was Paul Schehl (Germany), who was a close second in the short-track, that pushed the pace early along with Benjamin Kruger (Germany) but the chase was on behind, and ultimately the pair from Germany fell away from the podium places as Rouffiac, Andre Gallis, Halter and Gustav Pedersen (Denmark) passed the early leaders, with Kruger finishing in fifth and Schehl in sixth.For winner Rouffiac it was a well-timed move to ramp up his results a level, as while the French rider had been on the podium a number of times at the World Cups this season the top step has been illusive, though he made the move up when it counted most.The 26.1km event over was the second event on Sunday, with Italy's Valentina Corvi taking the women's U23 title earlier in the day. The women's elite and men's elite XCO races later in the day rounded out competition at the UCI Mountain Bike World Championships.Alix Andre Gallis (France)Nicolas Halter (Switzerland)Gustaz Pedersen (Denmark)Benjamin Kruger (Germany)Alejandro Garcia Vazquez (Spain)Manen Rens van Teun (Netherlands)

item.title: Inside Meta’s push to put robots to work in data centers
item.author: Paresh Dave, WIRED.com
item.content:encoded: Meta is testing robots that can plug in cables, reset servers, and handle other tasks inside its data centers, according to several current and former workers familiar with the projects. The ongoing effort, which has not been previously reported, may eventually allow Meta to operate its rapidly expanding data center footprint with fewer humans, keeping labor costs in check as its spending on AI infrastructure soars.Meta is using robots and related hardware from several different vendors, including Watney Robotics, Kinova, and ABB, according to the same workers, who asked to remain anonymous because they weren’t authorized to speak to the media. Kinova and ABB declined to comment. Watney didn’t respond to requests for comment.In one experiment, Meta is evaluating whether a Kinova Gen3 robotic arm could be used for power cycling or cutting off electricity to servers. The company is also testing a different robot to swap networking cables. One Meta data center worker estimates that if it’s successful, the bot could replace up to 80 percent of some people’s workloads. “We thought those of us performing the physical tasks were safe for a while, but not anymore,” says the worker. “It’s coming for us all, unfortunately.”

item.title: ‘It’s therapy by stealth’: the adult fans helping Lego build its billions in sales
item.author: George Francis Lee
item.content:encoded: A growing number of people are rediscovering their love of plastic bricks in later life and boosting the Danish company’s bottom lineIn a cosy cafe in Kingston upon Thames on the outskirts of London, nine people gather in the early evening to drink and talk. To the casual observer it may look like a book club, but when the friends reach into their bags it’s not paperbacks they produce – but packs of Lego.Geoff Lay, who organised the gathering, worked in software development before recently starting Noble Brick, a Lego-focused events organisation.Continue reading...

item.title: 'Just be super aggressive and try and make him proud' – UAE Team Emirates-XRG recalibrate Vuelta a España goals after losing Tadej Pogačar
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: As the Vuelta a España gears up to continue without former leader Tadej Pogačar on stage 9, his UAE Team Emirates-XRG teammates have spoken for the first time about the circumstances of the crash, the aftermath within the team, and their plans for the rest of the race.The entire UAE squad waited for their leader when he hit the deck 32km from the end of stage 8, eventually crossing the finish line in Xeraco despondently, 11:33 down with Pogačar out of the Vuelta and on the way to hospital.Now, the remaining seven riders – including João Almeida, Pavel Sivakov, and Jay Vine – will have to recalibrate their objectives. Stage wins seem to be the new goal, with none of the seven high up in the overall standings."After the stage, we were all like – I think you could see us crossing the line all together, really down. It was not the most joyful night, but it's how it is. It's cycling. It happens – not only to our team, to everyone," Pavel Sivakov told in Villajoyosa ahead of stage 9."But now we have to try to go for stages. I think we have good opportunities. Also today, it's a really hard stage, so it suits us really well. So we'll just keep fighting.""We have to fill in the shoes he left behind, just be super aggressive and try and make him proud."The American said there was "a weird tension" in the peloton throughout stage 8, which was beset by crashes from start to finish. It should have been a calm day of racing, but instead there was carnage."It's a flat sprint day when only two Burgos riders want to be in the breakaway. There's no wind, no nothing, it should be a super chill day," Vermaerke told ."Already from the neutral there's a crash, even the crash in the final, crashes before Tadej's crash – it was just a nervous day all around. It's never nice. Nobody wants to crash, nobody wants to go home on a day when it should be an easy day."There's probably a thousand rocks on the road that we ride through every day. At the end of the day, roads are just being closed an hour or two before. It's impossible to completely make a road clean for the 180km that we do every day. There's a bunch of rocks; I think it's hard to point out one specific one and blame that, so it's just really unlucky."While Vermaerke was riding ahead of Pogačar at the time of the crash, Sivakov was right behind him and had a clear view of what happened. He said nothing could have been done to avoid the fall."In the end, I was on Tadej's wheel when the crash happened. He was drinking his bottle and just hit this small object on the road and lost his balance, and yeah, nothing you could do for him," Sivakov told The Cycling Podcast."I think maybe if you had two hands on the handlebars, it would have been a different crash, because when you lose the bars with one hand, you're really exposed; you cannot really protect yourself."I think we were actually in a really good position, you know? We were taking a side of the road. I wouldn't say we were in a bad position, or we were a bit further back where it's a bit more dangerous where you cannot see what's coming up."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Train drivers secure 3.6% pay rise after threat of strikes on busy UK routes

item.content:encoded: Deal agreed between Avanti West Coast and Aslef is first to be approved by Burnham governmentTrain drivers have secured a significant pay rise after the threat of strike action was floated on busy routes across the UK, including on the busy London-Manchester line.The deal, which was agreed on Saturday between Avanti West Coast and the Associated Society of Locomotive Engineers and Firemen (Aslef) union, is the first to be approved by Andy Burnham in his premiership.Continue reading...

item.title: As it happened: GC takes major shift as red jersey solidifies his lead on La Vuelta stage 9
item.content:encoded: For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go! Hola and welcome to our live report of La Vuelta a España 2026 stage 9. The race looks very different after the events of yesterday which saw race leader Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) crash out. Now, Enric Mas (Movistar) leads the way.August 30, 2026 – 5:40 AMToday's stage is another brutal day at La Vuelta with six classified climbs including the final climb of the Alto de Aitana which is 22km long at 5.8%. The GC will surely see another big shake-up with more riders seeing a massive opportunity to challenge for the overall title. August 30, 2026 – 5:43 AMAs well as the battle for red, the battle for the blue and white KOM jersey is on with a big day of points available today. Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) leads the way ahead of green jersey holder Wout Van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) by just three points with plenty of climbs to come that will open the battle to more riders. August 30, 2026 – 5:51 AMYesterday, Mas refused to wear the red jersey after Pogačar crashed out...August 30, 2026 – 5:59 AMPogačar is remaining as positive as he can do after the crash with the world champion spending a few nights in Barcelona hospital.August 30, 2026 – 6:13 AMThe riders are all set and rolling at the neutral start. They have 6.4km of neutralised zone today. August 30, 2026 – 6:15 AMMas revealing the red jersey on the podium for the team presentation earlier...August 30, 2026 – 6:17 AMThe start of this stage is likely going to be chaotic with UAE Team Emirates-XRG being one of the teams who will be very keen to get up the road to chase stage wins after they all lost well over 11 minutes yesterday. August 30, 2026 – 6:26 AMSinuhé Fernandez (Burgos-Burpellet-BH) will wear the gold combativity number. August 30, 2026 – 6:27 AMRacing begins and there's no moves yet.August 30, 2026 – 6:28 AMFirst move comes off the front with Yevgeniy Fedorov (XDS-Astana) and Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) go away in a group of four. August 30, 2026 – 6:29 AMTobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility) is also in this lead group with about 20 riders trying to bridge the gap. August 30, 2026 – 6:30 AMAlexey Lutsenko (NSN) is the other rider in the front group. Two riders from Kazakhstan, one from Norway and one from Denmark. August 30, 2026 – 6:31 AMThe lead group grows with Jack Haig (Netcompany-Ineos), Michael Gogl (Alpecin-Premier Tech) and Domen Novak (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) involved. August 30, 2026 – 6:34 AMThe lead group grows so Lutsenko launches a move off the front and is now solo. August 30, 2026 – 6:38 AMLutsenko is back with Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility), Pavel Sivakov (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) and three others but another group made of five riders including two from UAE are coming across the gap. August 30, 2026 – 6:41 AMThe leading 6 have just 10" on the chasing 5 riders with a further 10" back to the peloton. This isn't getting away just yet. August 30, 2026 – 6:44 AMThis has the most climbing of any stage in this year's La Vuelta. 4940 metres of climbing. August 30, 2026 – 6:45 AMSantiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) is in the chase group. He lost time on the big climbing day in Andorra but has been showing that he's keen to get into breaks since then alongside teammate Pello Bilbao. August 30, 2026 – 6:47 AMRed Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe have been very keen on getting Gianni Vermeersch into the breakaway. He attacks for the second time today. August 30, 2026 – 6:48 AMStill only 24" up to the leaders. They are working well together but the battling to get up the road is far from over behind as Van Aert now starts to appear near the front of the peloton. August 30, 2026 – 6:53 AMThe gap eases out to 35" now but there are still plenty of attacks coming out of the peloton despite multiple teams trying to block the road. August 30, 2026 – 6:55 AMReuben Thompson (Lotto-Intermarché) and Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) in the chase gap at 34" with the peloton at 45". Not far away from the first climb of the day, the Puerto de Tárbena (7km at 5.4%).August 30, 2026 – 6:55 AMLennard Kämna (Lidl-Trek) is also in the chase group. August 30, 2026 – 6:57 AMFinally, the break may be allowed to go. The chasers are now at 40" behind the lead group but the peloton are now at 54". August 30, 2026 – 7:00 AMThe pace in the peloton changes again due to Van Aert hitting the front. He catches the chase group and is now leading the peloton at 38" from the leading six riders. August 30, 2026 – 7:03 AMInto the final 100 miles and it is Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe trying to get a new group going. Primož Roglič's team looks to have a plan today. Now 42" up to the break as Movistar are also getting involved in the attacking, as are Decathlon-CMA CGM. August 30, 2026 – 7:05 AMOnto the first climb of six today. The Puerto de Tárbena. The break now have 53" on the peloton as the chasing peloton stalls slightly with the leaders still working very well. August 30, 2026 – 7:06 AMBriefly looked like the peloton were happy but, despite having a rider in the break in the shape of Kron, Uno-X Mobility decided to kick things off again. August 30, 2026 – 7:07 AMBuitrago solo off the front of the peloton trying to bridge. August 30, 2026 – 7:09 AMFabian Weiss (Tudor) dropped from the lead group. August 30, 2026 – 7:10 AMFour riders fly out of the peloton and join Buitrago including Johannessen again. August 30, 2026 – 7:13 AMThe chasers have been caught again but Netcompany-Ineos launch a rider again with plenty keen to follow as Weiss is caught. August 30, 2026 – 7:15 AMSeveral riders dropped in the peloton including Jay Vine (UAE Team Emirates-XRG)August 30, 2026 – 7:17 AMPablo Torres another UAE rider dropped. Not great for them, but they do have Sivakov out front. August 30, 2026 – 7:18 AMValentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal-Quickstep) launching a new move with around 10 riders as Movistar and Decathlon-CMA CGM try to start controlling. August 30, 2026 – 7:19 AM1km to the top of the Puerto de Tárbena.August 30, 2026 – 7:21 AMKron leads over the Puerto de Tárbena.August 30, 2026 – 7:23 AMThe gap is still just 34" between the leaders and the head of the peloton as Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) is the latest to try and join the fun out front. August 30, 2026 – 7:25 AMBen Tulett (Visma-Lease a Bike) losing contact with the peloton unfortunately after coming down in he crash with Pogačar yesterday. August 30, 2026 – 7:26 AMParet-Peintre and Urko Berrade (Kern Pharma) join Fisher-Black in the chase of the leaders with a Tudor rider trying to join them. August 30, 2026 – 7:27 AMPablo Torres (UAE Team Emirates-XRG)The young Spaniard making his Grand Tour debut evidently struggling. August 30, 2026 – 7:28 AMMovistar now hit the front with Orluis Aular taking on the point of the bunch. They look like they may even be keen to go for the stage win with Mas looking really strong in the last few days in the mountains. August 30, 2026 – 7:30 AM1. Kron (UXM) 5pts2. Romele (XAT) 3ptsAugust 30, 2026 – 7:32 AMThis chase group has grown with Buitrago, Bruno Armirail (TVL), Stefan Kung (TUD), Embret Svestad-Bardseng (NCI) and many more joining the fun. August 30, 2026 – 7:35 AMThe first hour have seen the riders take on over 1000 metres of elevation with an average speed of 41.4kph. August 30, 2026 – 7:36 AMThe leaders still have 23" on the group of nine chasers with the peloton at 45". August 30, 2026 – 7:38 AMPart of the chase group have broken free and are joining the leaders. This may finally be the group allowed to go with 137km to go. August 30, 2026 – 7:41 AM11 riders now lead a group of 5 at 15" with the peloton at 45". August 30, 2026 – 7:43 AM14 riders now lead as the chasers join up with the front. August 30, 2026 – 7:44 AMThe gap to the peloton is looking like it may be around a minute with a few riders getting back in as the pace drops. August 30, 2026 – 7:45 AMMovistar lead the peloton but the break are working very well together. August 30, 2026 – 7:47 AMThere's another new chase group made up of about 10 riders including a Movistar rider. Very interesting that yet another move goes. August 30, 2026 – 7:48 AMFedorov (XAT)Double (JAY)I believe that is everyone involved with Double looking like the worst effected but all up and riding again. August 30, 2026 – 7:49 AMThe gap to the chase group is 1'04" with the peloton likely not too far behind. Pinarello-Q36.5 getting three riders involved in this chase group. August 30, 2026 – 7:52 AMMovistar are now taking full control of the peloton with a rider in the chase group as well with Raul Garcia Pierna. August 30, 2026 – 7:58 AMThe riders are 2km from the start of the next climb, the brutally hard Puerto de El Miserat which is a category 1 climb that is 5km long with an average of 10% with slopes hitting over 20%. The team cars will also be removed as the climb is very narrow. August 30, 2026 – 8:00 AMThe leaders are made up of 15 riders now with a gap of 1'34" to a group of 12. Then it is a further 1'49" to the peloton. The race looks like it has finally settled down. August 30, 2026 – 8:04 AMOnto the Miserat climb. Immediately a very narrow and dusty roads. August 30, 2026 – 8:05 AMThe peloton have let the break go. They are 3'38" down on the leaders. August 30, 2026 – 8:06 AMWalter Calzoni (Pinarello-Q36.5) has attacked the chase group to try and bridge the gap to the leaders. August 30, 2026 – 8:08 AMThe peloton dropping a lot of riders including the Monaco champion Victor Langellotti (XDS-Astana) who we would expect to be up there for longer than he has. August 30, 2026 – 8:13 AMMovistar have settled on holding the break at around 3'15" with Venezuelan champion Aular setting the tempo. August 30, 2026 – 8:17 AM1km to the top of the Miserat climb with Kevin Vermaerke (UAX) leading the front group. August 30, 2026 – 8:19 AMThe gradients are so steep they still have 350 metre of climbing this ascent.August 30, 2026 – 8:20 AMBuitrago attacks the lead group for the points and he takes them ahead of Sivakov and Lutsenko. August 30, 2026 – 8:24 AM1. Buitrago (TBV) 10pts2. Sivakov ((UAX) 6ptsThat sees Buitrago take the lead in the KOM standings by just 2 points over the man who wears the jersey, Andreas Leknessund (UXM). August 30, 2026 – 8:28 AMZana, Camprubi, Vader and Valter are now about 50" off the back of the leaders. That would be a great ride by them if they make it. August 30, 2026 – 8:33 AMThe Movistar led peloton ae still around 3'30". They really look like they are wanting to set things up for Mas to win in the leader's red jersey. To end the unwanted streak without a stage win for the Spanish squad at this race. August 30, 2026 – 8:38 AMMackellar has been dropped from the lead group with Calzoni joining it. His teammates of Camprubi and Vader aren't far away, either. August 30, 2026 – 8:39 AMHere is a view of what the riders have just been tackling on the previous categorised climb...August 30, 2026 – 8:40 AMOnto the next climb, the cat 3 Puerto de Tollos. 4km long at 5.8%. August 30, 2026 – 8:47 AMAt around the halfway point on the road. Movistar have let another minute slip away with 4'41" up to the leaders now with 98km to go. August 30, 2026 – 8:50 AMBuitrago snaps clear with a sharp acceleration and takes another max points on the Tollos climb. He leads Leknessund by 5 points now. August 30, 2026 – 8:53 AMThe gap continues to grow to 4'45". The stage still seems in the balance between the stage going to the break and a big GC challenge for the stage. It could go either way with the gap as it it. August 30, 2026 – 8:55 AMAnd the gap drifts beyond 5 minutes now. August 30, 2026 – 8:55 AMAttila Valter (TBV) is very close to getting onto the back of the lead group. August 30, 2026 – 9:00 AMIt is lunch time in the peloton. Several teams have riders back at the cars getting food for their riders. August 30, 2026 – 9:00 AM1. Buitrago (TBV) 3pts2. Calzoni (PQT) 2ptsAugust 30, 2026 – 9:03 AMMore riders are getting back in as we descend the climb. Vermeersch was dropped on the last climb on the steep gradients but is back in now as is Valter, Camprubi and the rest out front. August 30, 2026 – 9:08 AMThe lead group grows to 20 riders as they ride through the enxtremely rugged and dramatic landscape of the Serra Serella. August 30, 2026 – 9:11 AMVermaerke and Leemreize drop back to the cars from the lead group. Two former teammates with the American Vermaerke formally riding for Leemreize's Picnic-PostNL. And they do right being at the car, the temperature is above 34 degrees out there. August 30, 2026 – 9:14 AMMovistar continue to set the tempo in the peloton with around 5 minutes between the break and peloton. August 30, 2026 – 9:22 AMThe riders now head into the Sierra de la Carrasca. It is a very rugged looking part of the world. The leaders have just over 3km to the next climb of the cat 2 Puerto de Tudons (7km at 5.3%).August 30, 2026 – 9:29 AMIt will be very interesting to see how the GC battle goes for the rest of the race. The top 10 in GC is split by just over 6 minutes. However, the top 8 are split by under 4 minutes with Harold Tejada (XDS-Astana), Matias Skjelmose (Lidl-Trek), Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost), Oscar Onley (Netcompany-Ineos), Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike), Felix Gall (Decathlon-CMA CGM) and Primož Roglič (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) are all in with a shout to challenge Enric Mas (Movistar). August 30, 2026 – 9:30 AMKuss, who sits fourth at 2'15" off Mas, has won this race before. The year he won was the last time he had ridden all three Grand Tours in the same year. He is doing that again at this race. August 30, 2026 – 9:31 AMOf course, Roglič is the most experienced with four La Vuelta wins and five Grand Tour wins. He could get the out right record for wins in this race if he wins the red jersey in Granada. August 30, 2026 – 9:34 AMMovistar still leads behind just ahead of Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe and Decathlon-CMA CGM with the rest huddled behind them. The gap has come down a but to 4'33". August 30, 2026 – 9:37 AMCurrently just under 4km to the top of the Puerto de Tudons. August 30, 2026 – 9:39 AMIt does appear that Movistar are upping the pace in the peloton as they take another 10" off the time up to the leaders. August 30, 2026 – 9:42 AMThis picture gives a perfect view of the team order in the bunch. Movistar lead ahead of Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe, Decathlon-CMA CGM, Visma-Lease a Bike, Netcompany-Ineos, EF Edcuation-EasyPost and the rest. August 30, 2026 – 9:43 AMAll the riders ahead of the peloton have now come together to make a 24 man breakaway with 1.5km to go the top of the climb. Their gap continues to fall and is now 4'04". August 30, 2026 – 9:47 AM1. Buitrago (TBV) 5pts2. Calzoni (PQT) 3ptsAugust 30, 2026 – 9:49 AMThe gap up to the break now drops below 4 minutes for the first time in some time. August 30, 2026 – 9:53 AMThe gap just begins to grow again as Aular retakes the lead from Canal in the peloton.August 30, 2026 – 9:53 AMVictor Langellotti (XDS-Astana)August 30, 2026 – 9:57 AMAlessandro Romele (XDS-Astana)He's had enough of the breakaway and goes solo on the descent as a few riders have been taken out of the back due to the speed. August 30, 2026 – 9:59 AMRomele has put 45" into the rest of the break thanks to that superb descent by the Italian rider who is really a sprinter more than anything else. Very impressive. August 30, 2026 – 10:02 AMRomele takes the intermediate sprint with two chasers being Stefan Kung and Valentin Paret-Peintre, two riders that couldn't be more different. The big Swiss rider takes 2nd in the intermediate sprint and his French attacking partner takes 3rd. August 30, 2026 – 10:03 AMOnto the penultimate climb of the day now, the cat 2 Puerto de Benufallim with the climb being 5km at 5.8% with bonus seconds also available at the top. August 30, 2026 – 10:05 AMKung and Paret-Peintre have been caught as Sivakov attacks the group to try and get across the 49" gap to Romele who is riding superbly well at the moment. August 30, 2026 – 10:05 AMThe gap has cracked open back to the peloton with it now just over 6 minutes. August 30, 2026 – 10:07 AMThe lead for Romele is still go on this climb. As Camprubi sets off after the young Italian. August 30, 2026 – 10:08 AMAnd the front of the peloton changes. Decathlon-CMA CGM hit the front with two riders as Movistar were letting the gap drift a bit. This changes things yet again in the battle for the stage as well as the GC. August 30, 2026 – 10:10 AMCamprubi riding strongly in that Spanish champions jersey. He has closed to 20" to Romele already. August 30, 2026 – 10:11 AMSivakov and Vermaerke are pushing again in the chase group to try and continue to split things. August 30, 2026 – 10:12 AMAular sits up and is dropped by the peloton. That was a bit day at the front of the peloton but he did a superb job. August 30, 2026 – 10:14 AMOne of the UAE riders has got away from the rest and is trying to bridge across to Camprubi who is now stuck at 22" from a flying Romele. August 30, 2026 – 10:14 AMAnd it is Sivakov who joins Camprubi. August 30, 2026 – 10:16 AM1. Romele (XAT) 5pts 6"2. Sivakov (UAX) 3pts 4"August 30, 2026 – 10:22 AMSivakov and Camprubi are about to catch Romele with their gap at just 8" with the next chase group at 44" and the peloton at 5'50". August 30, 2026 – 10:22 AMRomele caught by Camprubi and Sivakov. August 30, 2026 – 10:27 AMThe chase group is now in bits with riders all over the road after one final uncategorised rise before a descent to the valley then 10km of flat before starting the final 22km climb of the Alto de Aitana. August 30, 2026 – 10:33 AMDecathlon-CMA CGM are using up Bastien Tronchon and Jordan Labrosse on the front of the peloton for the moment. 5'21" gap from them to the three leaders. August 30, 2026 – 10:37 AMRomele, Camprubi and Sivakov lead the chase group of 19 riders by 47" with the Decathlon-CMA CGM led peloton at 5'19". It is still all up for grabs with the Aitana looming in about 8km from now. August 30, 2026 – 10:40 AMThis leading trio have ridden superbly and now have a minute on the chase group. August 30, 2026 – 10:45 AMOnto the Alto de Aitana we go! 22km at 5.8% but with some brutal kicks in the second half in the restricted military zone. August 30, 2026 – 10:46 AMRomele, Sivakov and Camprubi have 1'23" on the chasers and 5'02" on the peloton. It isn't done for the peloton just yet. August 30, 2026 – 10:47 AMRomele can not follow Sivakov and Camprubi as they start the climb with around 50 minutes of climbing ahead. They take the chance to get the last few bottles of water before feeding closes. 38.5 degrees C out there. August 30, 2026 – 10:49 AMThe chase group are firing off attacks all the time with Buitrago and Lutsenko the first to really get a gap. August 30, 2026 – 10:51 AMDecathlon-CMA CGM are really upping the pace in the peloton now. The gap is falling rather quickly as they look to set up Felix Gall. August 30, 2026 – 10:57 AMSeveral riders losing touch in the peloton with Labrosse absolutely flying on the front for Gall. Jarno Widar (Lotto-Intermarché) really struggling at the back. August 30, 2026 – 10:58 AMDecathlon-CMA CGM have five riders still with Gall while the rest are struggling. Labrosse is riding the Movistar riders out of the train and he had to sit up briefly to allow his teammates across to him.August 30, 2026 – 11:00 AMWith 15km to go the two leaders have 1'05" on the first chasers then 1'31" to the second chase group. The peloton now at 3'36" with Labrosse still leading!August 30, 2026 – 11:01 AMLabrosse is finally done. Sander De Pestel takes over ahead of Leo Bisiaux, Callum Scotson, Matthew Riccitello and Gregor Muhlberger with Gall. August 30, 2026 – 11:02 AMThese two out front are riding well but there is a long way to go on this climb with the hardest gradients still to come. 🏁 15 km | Stage 9️⃣ - Etapa 9️⃣ | #LaVuelta26🤝 Sivakov and Camprubí are together in front with 1'30" on their direct chasers👊 Sivakov y Camprubí colaboran en cabeza. Los perseguidores, a minuto y medio⏱️ 3'48" Pelotón— @lavuelta.bsky.social (@lavuelta.bsky.social.bsky.social) 2026-08-30T15:01:48.384ZAugust 30, 2026 – 11:07 AMSivakov and Camprubi are still pushing hard but the peloton are now at 2'45" with over 10km to go. It looks like the GC will fight for the stage after all!August 30, 2026 – 11:09 AMRiders getting the last feed as, due to the heat, the cut off was 10km to go today. 2'22" between the leaders and the peloton now. August 30, 2026 – 11:10 AMRiccitello now takes over the pace setting in the peloton. August 30, 2026 – 11:10 AMSivakov gaps Camprubi but with just over 2 minutes to the GC riders it may not be enough. August 30, 2026 – 11:11 AMCamprubi isn't done yet and comes back to Sivakov. August 30, 2026 – 11:11 AMBisiaux takes over from Riccitello in the peloton with Muhlberger waiting to take on the final turn for Gall before they launch the Austrian GC rider. August 30, 2026 – 11:12 AMSivakov now does definitively gap Camprubi. August 30, 2026 – 11:14 AMMuhlberger takes over. He is in flying form for Gall and is in the top 10 on GC himself. This may see some major gaps begin to form. 1'48" up to Sivakov. August 30, 2026 – 11:16 AMAnother 10" clipped off Sivakov's gap as the pace continues to go up and up in the GC group. 1'31" between them now. August 30, 2026 – 11:17 AMKuss starting to lose a little bit of a gap as other riders lose tough and Sepp Kuss is distanced. August 30, 2026 – 11:18 AMEnric Mas follows with Primož Roglič, Oscar Onley and Richard Carapaz. August 30, 2026 – 11:19 AMMatias Skjelmose gets back in with the GC favourites. August 30, 2026 – 11:19 AM6km to go as Sivakov has 33" on Camprubi and 1'05" on the GC group.August 30, 2026 – 11:20 AMLots of riders get back into the GC group. August 30, 2026 – 11:20 AMWidar follows and pushes on himself as Skjelmose is dropped. August 30, 2026 – 11:21 AMHarold Tejada has got back in as well. August 30, 2026 – 11:22 AMMas, Gall, Roglič, Onley, Carapaz, Tejada, Widar.August 30, 2026 – 11:23 AMCamprubi and the rest of the break are caught with only Sivakov remaining. Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech) sits in after being caught from the break. August 30, 2026 – 11:24 AMThe Ecuadorian has stolen a march here with the rest not reacting at all. This is how he won the Giro, of course. He catches Filippo Zana who was in the gap. August 30, 2026 – 11:24 AMWidar tried a little move but he was heavily marked. No-one is pushing to join Carapaz who now has Sivakov in his sights. That is 5 minutes at the bottom of this climb almost closed. August 30, 2026 – 11:25 AMHe gets a gap and Mas flies across the gap to the white jersey with Gall unable to react to it. August 30, 2026 – 11:26 AMCarapaz catches Sivakov along with a surprising appearance from Buitrago, but all the GC riders come back again with 4km to go. August 30, 2026 – 11:27 AMHe was in the gap but wasn't reported. Gall closes him down and gets a gap for the first time but Mas just eases out of the saddle and closes him down again. August 30, 2026 – 11:27 AMWidar, Sivakov and Buitrago all distanced for now. August 30, 2026 – 11:29 AMOnley, Roglič follow well. Mas was poorly placed but responded well with Carapaz having to work harder to close. Widar and Lorenzo Fortunato (XDS-Astana) get back in as does Buitrago with Skjelmose and Tejada not far off. August 30, 2026 – 11:30 AMMatias SkjelmoseHarold TejadaThey get back in and immediately attack. Buitrago tries to join but he is followed by Gall and the rest as Gall kicks off again. August 30, 2026 – 11:31 AMThe red jersey launches and leaves everyone behind. The Spaniard does has Onley chasing him down, though. The man from Kelso joins the Spanish favourite with just under 3km to go. August 30, 2026 – 11:31 AMWidar is the man leading the chase behind them with Roglič as the rest are struggling to close up to the Slovenian. August 30, 2026 – 11:32 AMRoglič now pushing on to try and get across to Mas and Onley who are working together. Widar able to stay with Roglič, though. August 30, 2026 – 11:32 AMRoglič leaving Widar behind and is closing in on Mas and Onley. August 30, 2026 – 11:33 AMRoglič makes it across to Mas and Onley with 18" back to Gall and the rest. August 30, 2026 – 11:33 AMAs soon as Roglič got on the red jersey kicked hard to deaden his rival's legs but Onley is still with Mas with 1.5km to go. August 30, 2026 – 11:34 AM25" back to Gall and the rest now. This is quite the ride from Mas, Onley and perhaps expected from Roglič. August 30, 2026 – 11:34 AMAugust 30, 2026 – 11:36 AMMas continues to push to try and keep Roglič off the back but he isn't losing much. Onley is still locked onto Mas' wheel. Gall and co have 34" to close as Carapaz is just off the back of that group. 1'25" to Kuss. August 30, 2026 – 11:36 AM500 metres to go. Mas leads Onley with Roglič using everything to ramp up to close in on them but doesn't seem to be able to get there. August 30, 2026 – 11:37 AM250 metres to go and it will be between Mas and Onley today for the stage. August 30, 2026 – 11:38 AMEnric Mas of Movistar wins stage 9 of La Vuelta! He ends Spain's and Movistar's draught at the race and he definitively leads the race. August 30, 2026 – 11:38 AMMovistar's first win at La Vuelta for five years! August 30, 2026 – 11:55 AMSuperb ride by Mas but also from Onley as well. Roglič just 12" back then Gall at 18" then an epic ride by Cristian Rodriguez (XDS-Astana) leading in Skjelmose at 20". Widar at 25", Tejada 33", Carapaz 54", Buitrago rounds out the top 10 at 1'41". Kuss lost 1'44". August 30, 2026 – 12:00 PMMas now leads Roglič by 1'18" in the GC at the end of week one. Gall at 1'39", Onley at 2'20", Carapaz at 3'26", Skjelmose at 3'57", Kuss drops to 4'09", Tejada is at 4'39", Muhlberger still in the top 10 at 7'33" and 10th in GC at the end of the first week is young Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) at 8'05".August 30, 2026 – 12:10 PMAn incredible feeling for Mas. August 30, 2026 – 12:12 PMEnric Mas has a huge smile everywhere he goes now. August 30, 2026 – 12:15 PMSantiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) is the new KOM leader. August 30, 2026 – 12:17 PMOnley remains firmly in white by almost 6 minutes over Omrzel. August 30, 2026 – 12:37 PMAnd finally Wout Van Aert keeps his green jersey by 57 points over teammate Matthew Brennan. That said, Alessandro Romele closed to 65 points after winning the intermediate sprint today. August 30, 2026 – 12:39 PMTomorrow La Vuelta has a rest day before a brutal second week. But, today, it looks like Enric Mas could well go on to win his first ever Grand Tour with a magnificent victory.

item.title: UCI Mountain Bike World Championships: Valentina Corvi wins women's U23 XCO title
item.author: simone.giuliani@futurenet.com (Simone Giuliani)
item.content:encoded: Corvi went to the front early and stayed there, stretching the gap to 15 seconds by lap three and then crossing the line with a 43 second margin to Switzerland's Anina Hutter and a huge roar of celebration from the crowd."I knew from the moment I moved into the U23 category that the UCI World Championships would be held here," said Corvi. "At the beginning of the season I told my coach that we had to win, and I marked the date on the calendar straight away.""I am proud of myself and particularly happy with the progress I have made mentally. The crowd was fantastic and gave me an extra boost. At one point I could not feel the fatigue any more. I could only hear the people."Swiss rider Monique Halter was third at 1:55 behind the newly crowned world champion. Halter won the short-track title earlier on Thursday.It was the second time in this Championships that Corvi has gone to the podium to claim a rainbow jersey, with the U23 World Series leader who has such a big advantage she can already lay claim to the title, part of the winning Italian XC team relay squad.The 22.6km women's U23 race over 6 laps was the opening event on Sunday, with men's U23 race plus the elite women's and men's races running afterward and drawing the Mountain Bike World Championships to a close.Anina Hutter (Switzerland)Monique Halter (Switzerland)Fiona Schwibler (Switzerland) Rafaelle Carrier (Canada) Florencia Monsalvez Rojo (Chile)Mara Winter (Switzerland) Katrin Embacher (Austria)Bloeme Kalis (Netherlands)Bethany-Ann Jackson (Great Britain)

item.title: Women in UK arts feel they do not have equal opportunities for roles, says report
item.author: Rachel Hall
item.content:encoded: Exclusive: Research says sector is fixated with young talent, with most women experiencing unconscious bias or sexismWomen working in the arts believe they do not have equal opportunities for roles, especially as they get older, according to a report saying that the industry is fixated with “young and emerging” talent.Nearly all (95%) women working in the arts thought gender inequality persisted, while three-quarters (75%) reported experiencing unconscious bias or sexism, according to a survey of 76 arts professionals. More than two-thirds (69%) felt that age negatively affected their career success – a figure that rose to 100% among those working in artistic rather than managerial roles.Continue reading...

item.title: The final verdict on Formula E's Gen3 era
item.author: Sam Smith
item.content:encoded: Formula E will begin its fourth era of technical regulations later this year and it will be a huge step up in power that will affect the sporting landscape significantly until 2030 at least.How it got there is largely through the car that went before it, the Gen3, and since 2025, the Gen3 Evo. For good and bad, that car has informed Formula E's growth a great deal as the championship reaches a level of pace and power that will likely grab more and more fans' and investors' attention.Born during the Covid-19 pandemic era, as a project Gen3 was a massive challenge for the FIA and Formula E Operations. That was one that was largely met, but along the way there were myriad difficulties and flashpoints."Welcome to the farce." That was how one team principal greeted this writer walking through the paddock gates at Valencia in early December 2022.The Race had heard about the issues and accidents in private testing of the Gen3 car. Theo Pourchaire had ended up atop a sandbank at Calafat; Sam Bird, in a Jaguar-run car, had escaped a scary-sounding shunt at the same track; Oliver Rowland had bruised his legs in a crash at Mallory Park; and Mahindra's Lucas di Grassi severely damaged his car at Almeria. There were others too that were not quite as damaging.Why these accidents were happening was essentially because there were no rear traction brakes on the Gen3 cars. Through the design of the Gen3 it was deemed that regen and brake-by-wire systems would be enough. They weren't.If the powertrains hit issues and shut down, which they frequently did, drivers were left with zero braking capability as they headed for a wall (or, in the case of Pourchaire, a sandbank protecting a field).That salty paddock greeting from the team principal was still a shock though, because it was said with such disdain and resignation. At this point Formula E was in a real crisis, no doubt about it.Teams were unsure about the safety of their cars; drivers were actively worried and some manufacturers were even looking at their insurance and human resource compliance policies to see if they could legally compete knowing of the issues.All the while the opening race in Mexico City was just a few weeks away and there was no chance whatsoever of getting emergency braking systems fitted to the cars before they left Europe. Things were getting fraught. And then Sebastien Buemi wrote off his Envision-Jaguar in the Valencia test. This time it was public and all hell broke loose.Suddenly, there was open talk of the season opener being postponed. Meetings took place almost every hour at Valencia. A solution had to be found.Eventually it was with a secondary, solenoid-activated braking system applied for the second event in Saudi Arabia. It went some way to appeasing the teams and drivers. For Mexico City, extra Tecpro barriers were fitted to some corners. Despite this, Mitch Evans had a big shunt and for several hours Jaguar and Envision considered withdrawing. They were talked down.There were several other issues too. A shortage of spares was one other major obstacle to overcome. The fact that around nine cars were destroyed or significantly damaged (Max Guenther's Maserati at Diriyah; Edoardo Mortara (Maserati) and Pascal Wehrlein (Porsche) at Cape Town; and a quarter of the grid at Rome!) did little to help matters, but such was the conflation of the Gen3 cars with some gnarly tracks such as Rome and Diriyah that this level of chaos felt almost inevitable in the first season of the era.Just for extra pain, the teams and manufacturers were now working under a cost cap of €13million and €15m respectively across two seasons.When Mortara piled into Bird in Formula E's most cataclysmic ever accident in Rome, you could see the colour draining from his Maserari team principal James Rossiter's cheeks in real time. In a way that vision kind of encapsulated a wild west-like first Gen3 season."It was challenging but I think in the long-term memory of Formula E, Gen3 will be seen as a key step of the championship in terms of achieving a huge technological leap in efficiency."That is the verdict of FIA championship manager for Formula E, Pablo Martino, who tells The Race he believes the recovery from that 2022 and 2023 period was successfully pulled off.He's probably right, because by 2024 Formula E had more stability in all corners of the paddock. The Gen3 project had solidified, the racing was generally very good, and Formula E had a new, dynamic and engaging CEO in Jeff Dodds, who replaced Jamie Reigle in June 2023.By the second season, the racing itself had developed past the initial inability of the cars to lay down the extra 50kW of attack mode power, largely because the spec tyres, supplied by Hankook, were so hard.This led to a new form of racing, peloton or pack racing. As drivers managed useable energy knowing that the attack mode would lose them track position, a weird type of high-speed queuing pursuit took effect.Races would then explode into life, and often carbonfibre shards too, when the pace quickened in relation to the energy targets being hit. Then the pace was unleashed and the action got really fraught, often resulting in cars running three or four abreast. It sometimes resembled a trippy kind of single-seater Talladega NASCAR scene.At some tracks it worked fine but at wide-open expanses such as Portland, Berlin and Misano, it became essentially a tactical contact sport with front wings (brittle on the original Gen3 car) scattered around the place like confetti."Yes, we had maybe chaotic races, but it was also one of the most exciting periods in terms of unpredictability on track and multiple winners or multiple champion possibilities," appraises Martino now."I think the playing field across the different teams has been really narrow and the competition has been really tight between them."I think that's going to be remembered well, and it will be considered as an important step for the Formula E progress, especially on the evolution of the car. "Season 9 to season 12 [the Gen3 period from 2023-26] is pretty significant on how the technology has evolved towards efficiency."The arrival of all-wheel drive with the Gen3 Evo car for 2024/25 went a long way to fixing the lack of overtaking in the high-power mode. And with the PitBoost energy top-up stops finally coming in for that same campaign, there was extra flexibility for the FIA with the sporting format - which it diluted somewhat for 2026 as it was clear to competitors, consumers and fans that the races were just too busy and chaotic.It is also important to remember that traction control limitations were lifted when all-wheel drive came into being in 2025, as they will be for Gen4. Deploying all the power into the wheels with no tyre slip changed the way drivers were conducting their races. This resulted in drivers such as Rowland, Wehrlein and Nick Cassidy really coming to the fore because they saw specific areas in which they could be tactically positive on gaining track position at crucial times.The Gen3 Evo period also came with an improvement of performance from the Hankook tyres. So too upgrades to the power units themselves."The fundamental part was the four-wheel drive mode, but I think it was a package of improvements too," says Martino."Because the pure laptimes did already improve as well. It was not only on attack mode during the qualifying session. The overall race performance has improved."Gen3 certainly created challenges for the teams, but they were mostly overcome.Will it be remembered fondly? Perhaps by the fans, yes. But by the drivers? Largely not. Many actively disliked Gen3 but that was probably born from the early, troublesome days more than anything."We have a much more robust structure today than the one we had in Season 9 [2023] and that is good for all future development of Formula E," adds Martino.In that sense, and in the circumstances of Gen3's birth, Martino is probably right. Gen3 feels already like a stepping stone to something really special with the potent Gen4 cars.All kids go through awkward stages growing up. Gen3 was Formula E's later teenage years when it was still discovering itself, still making occasional embarrassing mistakes at the school disco. Now it's time to properly grow up."I think we have grown together as a championship," concludes Martino."We have built on all this knowledge. Sometimes knowledge comes because of the challenges or things that were not predicted at the very beginning."But overall, I think it has been a really positive four years for the championship, and no one can deny that because it has seen a huge evolution in fan base and interaction with the fans."
